Why does Catalonia keep pushing for independence?
What is the relationship between Spain and Portugal?

Questions we will cover:
Alfonso IX's own life, and something about his descendants
The state of the kingdoms of León and Castile in Alfonso IX's time
How the Reconquista was carried out step by step
The historical opportunities for Iberian unification that were missed

zh: 苍水死而明亡
en: When Cangshui Died, Ming Fell
intro:
清末为了宣传革命，章太炎在《支那亡国二百四十二年纪念会》宣言中写道：
愿吾滇人，毋忘李定国；
愿吾闽人，毋忘郑成功；
愿吾越人，毋忘张煌言；
愿吾桂人，毋忘瞿式耜；
愿吾楚人，毋忘何腾蛟；
愿吾辽人，毋忘李成梁。

张煌言在明末抗清斗争中起到了关键作用。本次分享将介绍他的活动，讨论他的作品。

zh: 布鲁诺之死——不懂玄学和哲学的神父不是好科学家
en: The Death of Giordano Bruno
intro:
本次分享关于影响力巨大的思想家、哲学家布鲁诺的生平、作品、思想，以及围绕他被判火刑而死的原因产生的巨大争论。

引起兴趣的问题：
布鲁诺到底犯了什么罪会被判烧死？
中世纪的宗教裁判所到底是一个什么样的组织？
日心说最早是哥白尼提出的吗？
我们所知的“科学”概念是怎么起源的？和神学、经院哲学和神秘学有什么关系？

拟讨论的问题：
“什么是真理？”（福音书中审判官彼拉多问耶稣基督的问题）
理性和神启、科学和宗教是什么关系？
“现代社会”的主流世界观是如何一步一步形成的？
中世纪给现代社会造成了什么样的影响？有哪些遗产被保留，而哪些遗产被否定？
intro_en:
This session is about the life, works and thought of the hugely influential thinker and philosopher Giordano Bruno, and the great controversy over why he was burned at the stake.

Questions to spark interest:
What crime did Bruno commit that got him sentenced to be burned?
What kind of organisation was the medieval Inquisition?
Was Copernicus really the first to propose heliocentrism?
How did our concept of "science" originate? How is it related to theology, scholasticism and occultism?

Questions for discussion:
"What is truth?" (the question the judge Pilate asked Jesus Christ in the Gospels)
What is the relationship between reason and revelation, and between science and religion?
How did the dominant worldview of "modern society" take shape step by step?
What impact did the Middle Ages have on modern society? Which parts of its legacy have been kept, and which rejected?

zh: 南朝贵族的自我修养
en: How to Be an Aristocrat of the Southern Dynasties
intro:
一些引起兴趣的问题：
王谢是名声在外的世家大族，在历史上究竟出过一些什么人物？
对于南齐这个政权，你有什么印象？
“竟陵八友”是谁？他们是做什么凑到一起的？
南朝的寒门和高门是怎么划分的？
你对六朝文学有什么印象？六朝时期的文学家们有什么代表作品，取得了哪些发展？

作为琅琊王氏的一员，却经历了并不常见的家庭变故，王融的人生从一开始似乎就偏离了一个标准南朝贵族的剧本。然而在他不长的一生中，他用自己的努力重新“塑造”了一个优秀的南朝贵族，在这个期间又作为一时文坛领袖，为后世留下了“永明文学”这个宝贵的财富，影响了之后中国文学的发展走向。

尽管他没能在政治上推动与他意气相投的贵族王子萧子良登上王位，他的朋友萧衍最终还是开启了贵族化的南梁。然而，这个南朝贵族掌舵的南梁政权在侯景之乱中光速陨落，南朝的贵族也受到了北方人的嘲笑。

王融的追求，是不是从一开始就有什么问题？贵族化的南朝衰亡是不是一种必然？

在本期活动之后我们还可以讨论这样一些问题：
为什么作为当时的文坛领袖，王融的名气后来却不如同为竟陵八友的谢朓，沈约等人？
一个人所处的时代会怎样影响TA对文学作品的评价？
我们该怎么看音韵声律和引用典故在文学欣赏上的意义？
intro_en:
Some questions to spark interest:
The Wang and Xie were famously illustrious great clans; what notable figures did they actually produce in history?
What impression do you have of the Southern Qi regime?
Who were the "Eight Friends of Jingling"? What brought them together?
How were humble families and great families distinguished in the Southern Dynasties?
What impression do you have of Six Dynasties literature? What are the representative works of Six Dynasties writers, and what advances did they make?

As a member of the Wang clan of Langya who nonetheless suffered an unusual family misfortune, Wang Rong's life seemed from the very start to stray from the script of a standard Southern Dynasties aristocrat. Yet in his short life he used his own efforts to "reshape" himself into an exemplary Southern aristocrat, and as a leading literary figure of his day he left posterity the precious legacy of "Yongming literature", which influenced the later course of Chinese literature.

Although he failed to help Prince Xiao Ziliang, a like-minded aristocrat, onto the throne, his friend Xiao Yan eventually founded the aristocratic Southern Liang. But this Liang regime, steered by the southern aristocracy, collapsed at lightning speed in the Hou Jing Rebellion, and the southern aristocrats became a laughing stock to the northerners.

Was there something wrong with what Wang Rong pursued from the very beginning? Was the fall of the aristocratic Southern Dynasties inevitable?

After this session we can also discuss questions such as:
Why, though he was the literary leader of his time, did Wang Rong later become less famous than his fellow Eight Friends of Jingling such as Xie Tiao and Shen Yue?
How does the era a person lives in shape how they judge works of literature?
How should we regard the significance of tonal prosody and literary allusion in appreciating literature?

zh: 伟大的足迹——来自摩洛哥的神秘旅者
en: The Great Footsteps: A Mysterious Traveller from Morocco
intro:
引起兴趣的问题：
- 你青年时代读过《经行记》《天方夜谭》《马可波罗游记》吗？
- 辛巴达的故事是如何迭代的？
- Baṭūṭah和Batu有什么词源联系？
- 郑和下西洋的航海路线是如何得知的？

分享的问题：
- 伊本·白图泰是如何走过四十四个国家的？
- 为什么在十四世纪远距离旅行可以实现？
- 白图泰如何到访中国？留下什么印象？
- 海陆丝绸之路如何兴衰迭起？
intro_en:
Questions to spark interest:
- Did you read the Jingxing Ji, The Arabian Nights or The Travels of Marco Polo when you were young?
- How did the stories of Sinbad evolve over time?
- Is there an etymological link between Baṭūṭah and Batu?
- How do we know the routes of Zheng He's voyages to the Western Oceans?

Questions we will cover:
- How did Ibn Battuta travel through forty-four countries?
- Why was long-distance travel possible in the fourteenth century?
- How did Ibn Battuta come to visit China? What impressions did he leave?
- How did the overland and maritime Silk Roads rise and fall in turn?

zh: 克吕尼，还是卡诺莎——中世纪教会拾遗
en: Cluny or Canossa: Gleanings from the Medieval Church
intro:
引起兴趣的问题：
- 中世纪是“黑暗”的吗？原始多神教的野蛮人是“高贵”的吗？
- 罗翔教授挂在嘴边的“圣奥古斯丁”真的那么伟大吗？
- 为什么欧洲交换生项目起名“伊拉斯谟计划”？
- “奥卡姆剃刀”里的奥卡姆是谁？

将要分享的问题：
- 安瑟伦，阿奎那，司各脱，胡斯，加尔文……这些人都是谁？
- “和子”问题是怎么发生并延续至今的？
- 修院制度是怎么发展和改革的？
- 大翻译运动和经院哲学的发展有何意义？
intro_en:
Questions to spark interest:
- Were the Middle Ages really "dark"? Were the primitive polytheistic barbarians really "noble"?
- Is the "St Augustine" that Professor Luo Xiang is always quoting really that great?
- Why is the European exchange programme called the "Erasmus Programme"?
- Who was the Ockham of "Ockham's razor"?

Questions we will cover:
- Anselm, Aquinas, Scotus, Hus, Calvin... who were all these people?
- How did the Filioque controversy arise, and why does it continue to this day?
- How did monasticism develop and reform?
- What was the significance of the great translation movement and the development of scholasticism?

zh: 第一巴图鲁——金帐汗国的前世今生
en: The First Baatar: The Golden Horde, Before and After
intro:
电视剧《雍正王朝》中，康熙问弘历：皇爷爷一生射杀了那么多野兽，是对还是不对？弘历答：这是皇爷爷不忘本，皇爷爷如果没有射杀这么多猛兽的本领，就不能平三藩，收台湾，平定蒙古叛乱，皇爷爷是我大清的第一巴图鲁！

引起兴趣的问题：
- 什么是蒙古？
- 蒙古和突厥是什么关系？
- 巴图鲁这个词是怎么来的？

将要分享的问题：
- 蒙古是怎么形成的？
- 拔都是如何建立金帐汗国的？
- 兀鲁思，八思哈，达鲁花赤都是什么意思？
- 金帐汗国在东欧进行了什么特别军事行动？
intro_en:
In the TV series Yongzheng Dynasty, the Kangxi Emperor asks Hongli: "Your grandfather has killed so many wild beasts in his life. Was that right or wrong?" Hongli replies: "It shows that Grandfather has not forgotten his roots. Had Grandfather not had the skill to kill so many fierce beasts, he could not have put down the Three Feudatories, taken Taiwan and crushed the Mongol rebellions. Grandfather is the First Baatar of our Great Qing!"

Questions to spark interest:
- What is "Mongol"?
- What is the relationship between the Mongols and the Turks?
- Where does the word "baatar" come from?

Questions we will cover:
- How did the Mongols take shape?
- How did Batu found the Golden Horde?
- What do ulus, basqaq and darughachi mean?
- What "special military operations" did the Golden Horde carry out in Eastern Europe?

zh: 鹅组大战孙吧——中文互联网的男女对立和信息茧房
en: Gender Wars and Echo Chambers on the Chinese Internet
intro: 我倒，原来你也在网上冲浪？
intro_en: Whoa, so you surf the web too?

zh: 漫威恩仇录——杰克·科比和斯坦·李
en: The Marvel Feud: Jack Kirby and Stan Lee
intro:
你一定看过漫威的电影，也知道斯坦·李这个名字。但漫威和那些经典的超级英雄形象真的是斯坦·李创造出来的吗？如果不是的话，为什么斯坦·李每次都会在漫威电影里出现呢？

这次分享，我们会讲述漫画家杰克·科比的故事，还有他和斯坦·李的爱恨情仇。我们会挖掘蜘蛛侠、美国队长、X战警这些经典形象的起源，他们是如何被创作出来的，后来又是如何发展的。我们也会探讨漫画行业究竟如何运作。在漫画这个行业中，到底有多少官司，多少背刺，多少尔虞我诈，多少反目成仇。

本次演讲的关键词有：诺曼底，儿童邪典，审查机制，版权，漫画家公会，逃离德黑兰，虐待老人罪。如果你是美国漫画迷和电影迷，一定不要错过。
intro_en:
You've surely seen Marvel films and know the name Stan Lee. But did Stan Lee really create Marvel and all those classic superheroes? And if not, why does Stan Lee turn up in every Marvel film?

In this session we will tell the story of the comic artist Jack Kirby and his tangled relationship of love and hate with Stan Lee. We will dig into the origins of classic characters such as Spider-Man, Captain America and the X-Men: how they were created and how they later developed. We will also look at how the comics industry actually works. Just how many lawsuits, how many betrayals, how much scheming and how many bitter falling-outs has this industry seen?

Keywords for this talk: Normandy, creepy children's content, censorship, copyright, the cartoonists' guild, Argo, elder abuse. If you're a fan of American comics and films, don't miss it.

zh: 诗学和诗艺：诗，戏剧和古希腊文学轶事
en: Poetics and Poetry: Verse, Drama and Tales of Ancient Greek Literature
intro:
本次分享聊一聊古希腊戏剧，其中具有代表性的系统论述，亚里士多德《诗学》以及贺拉斯《诗艺》。

引起兴趣的问题：
- 希腊神话构建了一个什么样的世界观？
- 现代故事中有哪些耳熟能详的希腊元素故事？
- 希腊戏剧有哪些不同的种类？
- “你下贱的品行犹如希腊戏剧的主角一般”，为什么有这种骂人的方式？

将要讨论的问题：
- 希腊罗马时代有哪些文学家？
- 戏剧是如何发展起源的？
- 亚里士多德和贺拉斯关于戏剧的理解有何不同？
- 古希腊是不是伪史？
intro_en:
This session talks about ancient Greek drama and its representative systematic treatments, Aristotle's Poetics and Horace's Ars Poetica.

Questions to spark interest:
- What kind of worldview did Greek mythology construct?
- Which familiar modern stories contain Greek elements?
- What different kinds of Greek drama were there?
- "Your base conduct is just like a hero of Greek drama": why would anyone insult someone that way?

Questions for discussion:
- Who were the writers of the Greek and Roman era?
- How did drama originate and develop?
- How do Aristotle's and Horace's understandings of drama differ?
- Is ancient Greece a fabricated history?

zh: 八字算命在算些什么？——中国人认识世界的一种复杂系统
en: What Does Bazi Fortune-Telling Compute? A Chinese System for Knowing the World
intro:
日常生活中我们可能听过“八字不合”“流年不利”“红鸾星动”等说法，这些玄学意味的套语已经成为了中国民俗的一部分。而“穷算命，富烧香”更是道出了一般人求诸算命的普遍心理。

那么，影响中国人至少几百年的八字命理，到底在算些什么？这个无比复杂精密的系统，是怎么来的？它体现了中国人世俗观念上怎样的价值取向？在现代社会有意义吗？它是“更符合中国宝宝体质的心理咨询”吗？

将要讨论的问题：
八卦系统和阴阳五行系统的差异和联系
农业社会对环境和季节的重视
什么叫“好命”：世俗价值观

引起兴趣的问题：
八字有多少种可能性？（MBTI有16种，星座有12个）
真的准吗？
大数据算命之可行性？
intro_en:
In daily life we may have heard sayings like "incompatible birth charts", "an unlucky year" or "the red phoenix star is stirring". These mystical set phrases have become part of Chinese folk custom. And the saying "the poor consult fortune-tellers, the rich burn incense" captures the common mindset of people who turn to fortune-telling.

So what exactly does bazi (Eight Characters) fortune-telling, which has influenced the Chinese for at least several hundred years, compute? Where did this extraordinarily complex and precise system come from? What values in everyday Chinese thinking does it reflect? Does it mean anything in modern society? Is it "psychological counselling better suited to the Chinese constitution"?

Questions for discussion:
The differences and connections between the Eight Trigrams system and the yin-yang and Five Phases system
Agricultural society's close attention to environment and seasons
What counts as a "good fate": everyday values

Questions to spark interest:
How many possible bazi are there? (MBTI has 16 types, the zodiac has 12 signs)
Is it really accurate?
Is big-data fortune-telling feasible?

zh: 托尔金和孕育指环王的牛津读书社
en: Tolkien and the Oxford Reading Group That Nurtured The Lord of the Rings
intro:
《指环王》是西方奇幻文学上最重要的里程碑之一。《指环王》系列的诞生和托尔金本人的学术道路和个人经历息息相关，其中最重要的孵化器是牛津大学一个叫做Inklings的社团（中文译为吉光片羽社、墨象社或者淡墨社）。许多英国著名作家、戏剧家、诗人都是这个社团的成员，其中最有影响力的就是托尔金和《纳尼亚传奇》的作者、基督教护教作家C.S. Lewis。

引起兴趣的点：
《指环王》的创作与托尔金的学术背景、神学思想和个人经历有何关系？
《指环王》中的霍比特人、佛多、山姆、甘道夫的人物形象可能的来源是什么？
托尔金对贝奥武夫的研究产生了什么影响？
牛津大学的Inklings社团中有哪些人？平时聚会干什么？对《指环王》系列的创作有何影响？

可以讨论的问题：
西方奇幻文学和中世纪的历史和文学有些什么有意思的联系？
牛津Inklings社团和烟霞有什么相似和不同的地方？
指环王、纳尼亚传奇、哈利波特、冰与火之歌之类的奇幻文学为什么这么火？
intro_en:
The Lord of the Rings is one of the most important milestones in Western fantasy literature. Its creation was closely tied to Tolkien's academic path and personal experience, and its most important incubator was an Oxford group called the Inklings (variously rendered in Chinese as "Jiguang Pianyu She", "Moxiang She" or "Danmo She"). Many famous British writers, dramatists and poets were members, the most influential being Tolkien and C.S. Lewis, author of The Chronicles of Narnia and a Christian apologist.

Points of interest:
How is the writing of The Lord of the Rings related to Tolkien's academic background, theological thought and personal experience?
Where might the characters of the hobbits, Frodo, Sam and Gandalf have come from?
What influence did Tolkien's scholarship on Beowulf have?
Who belonged to the Inklings at Oxford? What did they do at their gatherings? How did they influence the writing of The Lord of the Rings?

Questions we could discuss:
What interesting connections are there between Western fantasy literature and medieval history and literature?
How are the Oxford Inklings similar to and different from Yanxia?
Why are fantasy works like The Lord of the Rings, The Chronicles of Narnia, Harry Potter and A Song of Ice and Fire so popular?

zh: 端午祭——屈原贾生列传
en: For the Dragon Boat Festival: The Lives of Qu Yuan and Jia Yi
intro: 借着端午节重温一下屈原和贾谊的生平、文学成就。
intro_en: On the occasion of the Dragon Boat Festival, we revisit the lives and literary achievements of Qu Yuan and Jia Yi.

zh: 这是我的战争——萨拉热窝围城战
en: This Is My War: The Siege of Sarajevo
intro:
本次分享讨论南斯拉夫的兴衰往事，以及解体后最惨烈的萨拉热窝围城战。

引起兴趣的问题：
- 你玩过《这是我的战争》吗？
- 你听说过南斯拉夫吗？对南斯拉夫有什么印象记忆？
- 南斯拉夫有哪些宗教和种族问题？南斯拉夫的强邻们为此做出了什么贡献？
- 你还知道有哪些对平民造成巨大伤亡的围城战役？

将要讨论的问题：
- 南斯拉夫是如何建立，又为何分裂的？
- 波黑在南斯拉夫中处于什么地位？
- 萨拉热窝围城战为何而起？
- 萨拉热窝围城战中有哪些故事？
intro_en:
This session discusses the rise and fall of Yugoslavia and the most brutal episode after its break-up, the Siege of Sarajevo.

Questions to spark interest:
- Have you played This War of Mine?
- Have you heard of Yugoslavia? What impressions or memories do you have of it?
- What religious and ethnic problems did Yugoslavia have? What did Yugoslavia's powerful neighbours "contribute" to them?
- What other sieges do you know of that caused huge civilian casualties?

Questions for discussion:
- How was Yugoslavia founded, and why did it break apart?
- What was Bosnia and Herzegovina's place within Yugoslavia?
- Why did the Siege of Sarajevo happen?
- What stories came out of the Siege of Sarajevo?

zh: 旧金山亚裔移民故事：Japantown
en: Asian Immigrant Stories of San Francisco: Japantown
intro:
旧金山目前超过三分之一的居民是亚裔，包括中国人、日本人和菲律宾人。为什么这个城市聚集了这么多亚裔？还产生了全美最大的Chinatown和Japantown？他们是出于什么原因来到这个陌生的城市谋生？融入的过程中又遭遇了哪些心酸，甚至是迫害？这个城市本身的面貌又是如何被亚裔移民改造的？本次分享会将从旧金山的Japantown入手，介绍旧金山亚裔移民和城市变迁的故事。

引起兴趣的问题：
- 旧金山为什么有最大的Chinatown和Japantown？
- 为什么旧金山对日本人来说非常重要？
- 曾经旧金山最多元化、住满各种少数族裔的Fillmore District为什么销声匿迹了？
- 旧金山曾经的Manilatown（菲律宾裔社区）是怎么消失的？
- 西海岸的日本人在二战期间为什么被关入集中营？他们在集中营的生活是怎样的？战后他们是怎么重建自己的家园的？
- 六七十年代的民权运动中，日本人是如何参与争取平权的？
- 美国历史上对亚裔都有哪些歧视性的法律？当时的人如何在那种环境下生存下来？这些法律又是什么时候废除的？
intro_en:
More than a third of San Francisco's residents today are Asian American, including Chinese, Japanese and Filipino Americans. Why has this city attracted so many Asians, and even given rise to the largest Chinatown and Japantown in the United States? What brought them to this unfamiliar city to make a living? What hardships, and even persecution, did they face as they tried to fit in? And how did Asian immigrants transform the city itself? Starting from San Francisco's Japantown, this session will tell the story of the city's Asian immigrants and how the city has changed.

Questions to spark interest:
- Why does San Francisco have the largest Chinatown and Japantown?
- Why is San Francisco so important to the Japanese?
- Why did the Fillmore District, once San Francisco's most diverse neighbourhood and home to all kinds of minorities, disappear?
- How did San Francisco's former Manilatown (the Filipino community) vanish?
- Why were Japanese Americans on the West Coast sent to internment camps during the Second World War? What was life like in the camps? How did they rebuild their homes after the war?
- How did Japanese Americans take part in the fight for equal rights during the civil rights movement of the 1960s and 70s?
- What discriminatory laws against Asians have there been in American history? How did people survive in that environment? When were these laws repealed?

zh: 殊途同归——从“渤海高氏”一窥汉唐之间的士族
en: Different Roads, Same End: The Gao of Bohai and the Great Clans between Han and Tang
intro:
一些引起兴趣的问题：
你知道什么出身于“渤海高氏”的著名历史人物吗？
“渤海高氏”活跃在什么样的时间和空间里？
“渤海高氏”的成员都是哪里人？他们是渤海人吗？他们是汉族/华夏族人吗？他们是“中国”人吗？
你还知道什么历史上著名的士族吗？

把大象装进冰箱里，需要三个步骤。那么，把一个家族变成皇族，又需要几个步骤呢？从一个地方上的名门，到一个远近闻名的望族，再到君临天下的帝胄，不同的发展阶段，会让一个士族家族遇到什么样的环境？面临什么样子的抉择？

在本期活动里我们还可以讨论这样一些问题：
什么样的家族会被称为士族？
士族产生，发展和巩固的基础都是什么？
士族是以什么样的方式影响社会和历史的？
不同的士族家族之间会有什么样的不同？这些不同点又是如何产生的？
intro_en:
Some questions to spark interest:
Do you know any famous historical figures from the "Gao clan of Bohai"?
In what time and place was the "Gao clan of Bohai" active?
Where were the members of the "Gao clan of Bohai" from? Were they from Bohai? Were they Han/Huaxia? Were they "Chinese"?
What other famous great clans in history do you know of?

Putting an elephant in a fridge takes three steps. So how many steps does it take to turn a family into an imperial house? From a local notable family, to a renowned great clan, to emperors ruling all under heaven: what circumstances does a great clan meet at each stage of its development, and what choices does it face?

In this session we can also discuss questions such as:
What kind of family counts as a great clan?
What were the foundations on which great clans arose, developed and consolidated their position?
In what ways did great clans influence society and history?
How did different great clans differ from one another, and how did those differences come about?

zh: 英雄还是恶魔——张献忠
en: Hero or Devil: Zhang Xianzhong
intro:
在明末大乱世中，张献忠似乎永远是一个配角，而且形象大多不好。在农民军眼里，张献忠是一个时降时叛的机会主义者。在明清官方眼里，张献忠是个聚众作乱的逆贼。在四川的民间传说中，张献忠是一个杀人如麻的屠夫，恐怖的凶神。在小说《李自成》和电影《双雄会》中，张献忠也是奸诈、残暴的代名词。张献忠到底是一个什么样的人？他为什么可以一度成为农民起义军的最强力量？大西政权后来到底是如何灭亡的？

“天生万物与人，人无一物与天，杀杀杀杀杀杀杀。”这句话让张献忠成为了一个meme，无数张献忠主题的表情包开始传播。可传说中的“七杀碑”真的存在吗？张献忠到底为什么杀人？他真的有一套自己的杀人哲学吗？

这次分享，我们不会以人物传记的模式讲解张献忠，也不会评价张献忠到底是功大于过，还是过大于功。而是试图放眼世界，对比古今。以张献忠为切入点，探讨张献忠生活的时代，反思张献忠的悲剧为什么在历史中一遍又一遍重演。李世民曾说：“夫以铜为镜，可以正衣冠；以史为镜，可以知兴替；以人为镜，可以明得失。”张献忠已经死去三百多年了，但我们仍然可以以张献忠为镜子，时时反思和警醒自己，不要犯张献忠的错误。

参考资料：
顾诚《明末农民战争史》
《明史·张献忠传》
古洛东《圣教入川记》
魏斐德《洪业：清朝开国史》
鲁迅《晨凉漫记》
郭沫若《甲申三百年祭》
intro_en:
In the great chaos of the late Ming, Zhang Xianzhong always seems to be a supporting character, and usually an unsavoury one. In the eyes of the peasant armies, he was an opportunist who kept surrendering and rebelling again. To the Ming and Qing authorities, he was a rebel who gathered mobs to rise up. In Sichuan folklore, he was a butcher who killed people by the thousands, a terrifying demon. In the novel Li Zicheng and the film Shuang Xiong Hui, Zhang Xianzhong is also a byword for treachery and cruelty. What kind of man was Zhang Xianzhong really? Why was he for a time the strongest force among the peasant rebel armies? And how did his Great Xi regime eventually fall?

"Heaven brings forth all things for man; man gives nothing back to Heaven. Kill kill kill kill kill kill kill." This line turned Zhang Xianzhong into a meme, and countless Zhang Xianzhong-themed reaction images began to circulate. But did the legendary "Seven Kills Stele" really exist? Why did Zhang Xianzhong kill? Did he really have a philosophy of killing of his own?

In this session we will not present Zhang Xianzhong in the form of a biography, nor judge whether his merits outweighed his faults or the other way round. Instead we will try to take a global view and compare past and present, using Zhang Xianzhong as a way into the era he lived in and reflecting on why his tragedy has been repeated again and again in history. Li Shimin once said: "With bronze as a mirror, one can straighten one's clothes and cap; with history as a mirror, one can understand the rise and fall of states; with people as a mirror, one can see one's own gains and losses." Zhang Xianzhong has been dead for more than three hundred years, but we can still use him as a mirror to reflect on and warn ourselves constantly, so as not to repeat his mistakes.

References:
Gu Cheng, A History of the Peasant War at the End of the Ming
History of Ming, "Biography of Zhang Xianzhong"
François-Marie-Joseph Gourdon, The Entry of the Holy Religion into Sichuan
Frederic Wakeman, The Great Enterprise: The Manchu Reconstruction of Imperial Order in Seventeenth-Century China
Lu Xun, "Random Notes in the Morning Cool"
Guo Moruo, "In Memory of the Tercentenary of 1644"

zh: 从摄关到武家——院政斗乱史
en: From Regents to Warriors: The Turbulent Age of Cloistered Rule
intro:
藤原道长在完成“一家立三后”的壮举后，咏出了“此世即吾世，如月满无缺”的和歌。然而，随着道长的去世，日本进入了一段动乱的年代。平安时代华丽的贵族社会逐渐落下帷幕，新兴的武士登上历史舞台。本期来聊聊道长人生登顶以后，平安时代后期各方势力的纠葛与斗争，直至武家政权的诞生，这其中曲折的脉络。

- 摄关政治是如何衰落的？
- 院政是什么体制？
- 武士是如何一步步发展，走向历史前台的？
- 平家繁华是怎样建成的？
- 源赖朝何以“翻盘”？
intro_en:
Having accomplished the feat of making three of his daughters empresses, Fujiwara no Michinaga composed the waka: "This world, I think, is my world; like the full moon, nothing is lacking." But after Michinaga's death, Japan entered an age of turmoil. The splendid aristocratic society of the Heian period gradually came to an end, and the rising warrior class stepped onto the stage of history. In this session we talk about the entanglements and struggles among the various powers of the late Heian period after Michinaga reached the pinnacle of his life, and the winding course that led to the birth of warrior government.

- How did regency government decline?
- What kind of system was cloistered rule?
- How did the samurai develop step by step and move to the forefront of history?
- How was the splendour of the Taira built?
- How did Minamoto no Yoritomo manage to turn the tables?

zh: 越石区区——刘琨的生前身后
en: Liu Kun, Before and After
intro:
本周补上上次因故缺席的第八十六期。本次分享将从刘琨POV切入两晋十六国时期的故事。

引起好奇的问题：
你听说过闻鸡起舞的故事吗？主角是谁？
五胡乱华是哪五胡？为什么会引起大规模的动乱？
“永嘉”代表着什么样的群体记忆？
“江左夷吾”是谁？对东晋作出了什么贡献？
桓温的名字有什么来历？

本次将要讨论的问题：
刘琨是如何“浪子回头”投身军政事业的？
刘琨有哪些著名的文学作品？
作为刘琨身后的延续，他的外甥温峤在东晋做出了哪些贡献？
苏峻之乱前后的东晋经历了什么动荡历程？
intro_en:
This week we make up for session 86, which was cancelled last time. This session will tell the story of the Jin dynasties and the Sixteen Kingdoms from Liu Kun's point of view.

Questions to spark curiosity:
Have you heard the story of "rising at cockcrow to practise the sword"? Who is its hero?
Who were the "Five Barbarians" who threw China into chaos? Why did they cause such widespread upheaval?
What collective memory does "Yongjia" stand for?
Who was "the Guan Yiwu of the lands east of the Yangtze"? What did he contribute to the Eastern Jin?
Where does Huan Wen's name come from?

Questions for discussion in this session:
How did Liu Kun, the "prodigal son", turn over a new leaf and devote himself to military and political affairs?
What are Liu Kun's famous literary works?
As the continuation of Liu Kun's legacy, what did his nephew Wen Jiao contribute to the Eastern Jin?
What turmoil did the Eastern Jin go through before and after the Su Jun Rebellion?

zh: 留下辞世句吧！——遗言文学
en: Leave a Death Poem! The Literature of Last Words
intro:
本次活动将分享各种有趣的临终遗言，从文学到梗到各种黑色幽默。

你知道哪些有意思的遗言？希望参与分享的朋友可以来一起讨论。

以下是一些例子：
“自由，多少罪恶假汝之名以行！”——罗兰夫人临刑前
“别碰我的圆！”——阿基米德对侵入的罗马士兵
“人生五十年，与天地长久相较，如梦又似幻。”——出自幸若舞《敦盛》，更因织田信长而闻名
“平生不修善果，只爱杀人放火。忽地顿开金枷，这里扯断玉锁。咦！钱塘江上潮信来，今日方知我是我。”——鲁智深临终偈
intro_en:
This session will share all kinds of interesting last words, from the literary to the meme-worthy to all sorts of black humour.

What interesting last words do you know? Friends who would like to share are welcome to join the discussion.

Here are some examples:
"O Liberty, what crimes are committed in thy name!" — Madame Roland before her execution
"Do not disturb my circles!" — Archimedes to the Roman soldier who burst in
"Man's fifty years, compared with the eternity of heaven and earth, are but a dream, an illusion." — from the kōwakamai Atsumori, made famous by Oda Nobunaga
"In life I never cultivated good deeds, but loved only killing and burning. Suddenly the golden shackles spring open, and here the jade chains are torn apart. Ah! The tide comes in on the Qiantang River; today at last I know that I am I." — Lu Zhishen's parting verse

zh: 身世浮沉雨打萍——夏威夷王国的兴亡
en: Adrift Like Duckweed in the Rain: The Rise and Fall of the Hawaiian Kingdom
intro:
第一次去夏威夷大岛时，注意到有个浮潜点叫做Captain Cook，搜了下发现原来现在这个著名的浮潜地点就是当初库克船长发现夏威夷群岛时停靠的地方，他自己也因为部落冲突丧命于此，这片海湾还成了夏威夷文化的“禁忌之地”。后来陆续了解到这里之前曾是一个独立自主，存续近百年的独立王国，创始人还被称为“太平洋上的拿破仑”。本次分享就来聊聊夏威夷群岛上曲折的故事，同时会介绍一些相关的历史遗迹和博物馆。

- 为什么夏威夷人要碰瓷拿破仑？
- 为什么夏威夷王国成立后一直保持独立，从未成为英国殖民地，国旗却是米字旗？
- 夏威夷王国主权的丧失为什么说是一个持续了百年的过程？
- 美国如何施加对夏威夷的影响，和美国外交路线的摇摆有什么关系？
- 夏威夷的蔗糖产业如何被美国反复横跳的关税改革玩坏的？
- 夏威夷王国具体是被谁颠覆的？他们为什么有这个政治权利？具体通过什么方式？
- 华人（包括孙中山家族）如何在夏威夷发展壮大，以至于成了晚清民国革命党的重要据点？
- 现在各个岛屿分别都有什么景点/博物馆下次旅行可以顺路看看？
- 现在夏威夷人如何看待这段历史？
intro_en:
On my first trip to Hawaii's Big Island, I noticed a snorkelling spot called Captain Cook. Looking it up, I found that this now-famous snorkelling site was where Captain Cook anchored when he came upon the Hawaiian Islands; he himself was killed here in a clash with the islanders, and the bay became a "forbidden place" in Hawaiian culture. Later I learned that the islands had once been an independent, self-governing kingdom that lasted nearly a century, and that its founder was even called "the Napoleon of the Pacific". In this session we will talk about the twisting story of the Hawaiian Islands and introduce some related historic sites and museums.

- Why did Hawaiians compare their king to Napoleon?
- Why did the Hawaiian Kingdom, which remained independent from its founding and never became a British colony, have the Union Jack on its flag?
- Why can the loss of Hawaiian sovereignty be described as a process that lasted a hundred years?
- How did the United States exert its influence on Hawaii, and how was this tied to the swings in American foreign policy?
- How was Hawaii's sugar industry wrecked by America's back-and-forth tariff reforms?
- Who exactly overthrew the Hawaiian Kingdom? Why did they have the political rights to do so? By what means?
- How did the Chinese (including Sun Yat-sen's family) grow and prosper in Hawaii, to the point that it became an important base for revolutionaries in the late Qing and early Republic?
- What sights and museums are on each island today that you could visit on your next trip?
- How do Hawaiians view this history today?

zh: 终究是战士——罗兰之歌
intro:
随着圣瓦伦丁节到来，我们本期分享同样与基督教相关的一部浪漫史诗《罗兰之歌》。罗兰之歌是法兰克武功歌中最著名的一部，对后世产生了深远的影响——在文艺复兴时期，意大利诞生了另一部作品《疯狂的奥兰多》。

引起好奇的问题：
你听说过什么著名的骑士故事？
亚瑟王故事的原型是什么？
欧洲还有哪些著名的史诗文学？
你所理解的骑士精神是什么？

将要分享的内容：
罗兰之歌的故事原型是什么？
加洛林故事集还有哪些独特的演绎？
罗兰在其他国家的传说故事中经历了怎样的流变？
在疯狂的奥兰多中，罗兰的形象发生了什么变化？
en: A Warrior to the End: The Song of Roland
intro_en:
With St Valentine's Day approaching, this session is about another work with Christian connections, the romantic epic The Song of Roland. The Song of Roland is the most famous of the Frankish chansons de geste and had a profound influence on later generations: in the Renaissance, Italy produced another work, Orlando Furioso.

Questions to spark curiosity:
What famous tales of knights have you heard?
What is the prototype of the Arthurian legends?
What other famous European epics are there?
What does chivalry mean to you?

What we will cover:
What is the historical prototype of The Song of Roland?
What distinctive retellings are there in the Carolingian cycle?
How did Roland's story change in the legends of other countries?
How did Roland's image change in Orlando Furioso?

zh: 愿将大袖遮天日，莫使春花任晓风——《源氏物语》的世界
intro:
《源氏物语》是世界上最早的长篇写实小说，成书于日本风雅绚烂的平安时代中期，代表了日本古典文学的巅峰。直至近代对《源氏物語》的各种改编诠释也愈加丰富，其中包括今年的大河剧，以作者紫式部故事为蓝本的《致光之君》。
《源氏物语》是怎样一部作品呢？它奠定了日本“物哀”的美学，作者紫式部作为一条天皇中宫藤原彰子的宫廷女官，以慧眼妙笔娓娓写就，描绘了主人公光华公子源氏，贵为皇子却因相士一言被降为臣籍、赐姓源氏，与许多被作者以花比拟，如花朵般各形各色，命运也如花般飘零易落的女性的种种爱恋。物语共五十四帖，长达百万言，在和歌、汉文、白（居易）诗、雅乐，四时节令，鸿雁往来，月影暗香——衣香鬓影中呈现的是一个风流闲雅，绚烂夺目，却也颓废虚幻，悲哀零落的平安贵族世界。后人也能从荣华的侧影中，瞥见王朝鼎盛时的权势起落，政治更迭。
但更多的是情。以物寄情，以景起情，以诗言情，以歌喻情。物语中所讲述的感情，有不知所起的暧昧，也有克制婉约的怀念，有超越伦理的悲恋，也有机缘天定的遇合，有稍纵即逝的浅情，也有凄厉刻骨的深情。本次分享我们将主要讲述光源氏与数位女性的故事，一窥其中的时代细节，人情欲望，与美学哲学。
我们也将介绍对比丰子恺与林文月的两种主要中文译本，及《源氏物语》及对其代表的风雅的向往怎样滋养了世纪初的中国网络社区及创作。
en: The World of The Tale of Genji
intro_en:
The Tale of Genji is the world's earliest full-length realist novel. Written in the middle of Japan's elegant and splendid Heian period, it represents the pinnacle of classical Japanese literature. Right up to the present, adaptations and interpretations of The Tale of Genji have grown ever richer, including this year's Taiga drama Dear Radiant One, based on the story of its author, Murasaki Shikibu.
What kind of work is The Tale of Genji? It laid the foundation of the Japanese aesthetic of mono no aware. Its author, Murasaki Shikibu, a lady-in-waiting to Fujiwara no Shōshi, empress to Emperor Ichijō, wrote it with a keen eye and a deft pen. It depicts the hero, the Shining Prince Genji, who, though born an imperial prince, was reduced to commoner status and given the surname Minamoto (Genji) on the word of a physiognomist, and his many loves with women whom the author likens to flowers: as varied as blossoms in form and colour, and with fates as fleeting and easily scattered as flowers. The tale runs to fifty-four chapters and about a million words. Through waka, classical Chinese, the poems of Bai Juyi, gagaku court music, the seasonal festivals, the exchange of letters, moonlight and subtle fragrances, amid rustling robes and elegant coiffures, it presents a Heian aristocratic world that is refined and leisurely, dazzlingly splendid, yet also decadent and illusory, sorrowful and fading. Readers can also glimpse, in the shadows of this glory, the rise and fall of power and the shifts of politics at the height of the court's prosperity.
But above all it is about feeling. Feelings entrusted to objects, feelings stirred by scenery, feelings expressed in poems, feelings conveyed through songs. The emotions in the tale range from ambiguous attractions that arise from who knows where to restrained, understated longing; from tragic loves that transgress morality to encounters ordained by fate; from fleeting shallow affections to piercing, unforgettable passions. In this session we will mainly tell the stories of Genji and several women, to glimpse the details of the era, human desire, and its aesthetics and philosophy.
We will also introduce and compare the two main Chinese translations, by Feng Zikai and Lin Wen-yueh, and look at how The Tale of Genji, and the longing for the elegance it represents, nourished Chinese online communities and creative work at the turn of the century.

zh: 打工人的杀妻往事——吴起列传
intro:
本次分享讲述战国时期军事家政治家吴起的生平，他吊诡的性格以及备受争议的杀妻行为。

引起兴趣的问题：
你听说过吴起这个人吗？印象中他是个什么样的人？
你知道东西方分别都有哪些杀父/母、杀子/女、杀妻/夫的故事？
“上岸第一剑，先斩意中人” 算不算一种现代意义上的杀妻/夫？
如何看待家长制（父权制）之下的亲缘关系谋杀等等的故事和背后的“情结”？
本次分享要讨论的内容：
吴起在战国时期起了什么作用？
吴起在政治军事上分别有什么建树？
杀父/母、杀子/女、杀妻/夫这类行为在各国神话传说中有何体现？
家长制和父权制有何细微差别？
en: A Working Man Who Killed His Wife: The Life of Wu Qi
intro_en:
This session tells the life of Wu Qi, military strategist and statesman of the Warring States period, his paradoxical character, and the much-debated killing of his wife.

Questions to spark interest:
Have you heard of Wu Qi? What sort of man do you imagine him to be?
What stories of killing one's father or mother, son or daughter, or wife or husband do you know from East and West?
Does "Once you've made it ashore, your first sword-stroke is for your sweetheart" count as a modern form of killing one's spouse?
How should we view stories of murder within the family under paternalism (patriarchy), and the "complexes" behind them?
What this session will discuss:
What role did Wu Qi play in the Warring States period?
What were Wu Qi's political and military achievements?
How are killing one's parents, children or spouse reflected in the myths and legends of different countries?
What is the subtle difference between paternalism and patriarchy?

zh: 刘易斯与克拉克远征 - 一个故事的几种讲法
intro:
“刘易斯与克拉克远征”在中文资料中出现较少。但在普通美国人的历史常识中，这一事件的知名度和重要性可以类比于“唐三藏西天取经”或者“张骞出使西域”，是一件被反复讲述、称颂的事件，并被赋予了“西进运动起点”的历史意义。

本次分享，主要介绍了
- 远征的动因和过程
- 环美旅行途中可以打卡的远征相关的历史地标和博物馆
- 在多个版本的叙述中，哪些是错误信息，又有什么信息被刻意强调或隐藏了？
- 印第安女性萨卡加维亚与美国女权运动的关联是？
- 这次远征到底是否算得上成功？
- 在向印第安人“宣扬和平”的问题上，历史是如何带来了巨大的讽刺？
- 这次远征与清王朝有着了怎样的关联？

鉴于涉及的历史背景较多，推荐参加活动前先花5分钟简单看一下：https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/刘易斯与克拉克远征
en: The Lewis and Clark Expedition: Several Ways to Tell a Story
intro_en:
The Lewis and Clark Expedition rarely appears in Chinese sources. But in the historical common knowledge of ordinary Americans, its fame and importance are comparable to Xuanzang's pilgrimage to the West or Zhang Qian's mission to the Western Regions: it is an event told and celebrated again and again, and has been given the historical significance of "the starting point of westward expansion".

This session mainly covers:
- The motives for the expedition and how it unfolded
- Historic landmarks and museums related to the expedition that you can visit on a road trip across America
- Across the many versions of the story, what is misinformation, and what has been deliberately emphasised or hidden?
- What is the connection between the Native American woman Sacagawea and the American women's rights movement?
- Can the expedition really be counted a success?
- On the question of "promoting peace" among the Native Americans, how did history deliver a huge irony?
- What connection did the expedition have with the Qing dynasty?

As there is a lot of historical background involved, we recommend spending five minutes skimming this before the session: https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/刘易斯与克拉克远征

zh: "这活动到底怎么了？"——2023年度总结
intro:
“烟霞”主题分享活动在2023年一共举行了41期。综合各期活动和反馈，这周利用活动的时间进行回顾和展望。活动发展成了什么样子？活动将朝着什么方向发展？
内容
独创性：
很多中文世界中不常提及、但非常有趣的小众话题——这像是在挖掘
很多在外语世界中广泛讨论、在中文语境中缺失的话题——这像是在翻译
一些分享者结合自己经历充满热情的独创分享——这是在创造，但可遇不可求
有一种历史地理套餐的感觉（32期与历史有关，其中29期地域特征非常明确）。很多期的模式是限定时间+限定地域的故事。比较流行的说法诸如微观史学、city walk。
网状叙事，不同期活动，相互呼应相互联系。经常可以听到分享者说：我们之前在XX期的分享中提到XX。
日本相关分享很多（共11期）。可能反映了日本在历史、文化、艺术方面确实做出了很大的努力。
形式
活动时间总是无法让所有人满意
公告发布的流程没有十分严格
宣传渠道波动很大
分享时间和讨论时间把控调节
值得讨论的现实和预期
知识性/学术性和独特性/娱乐性之间，需要平衡
日本相关话题疑似有点多了（约11期是日本相关话题，占了1/4）
历史话题确实多了（只有9期与历史无关，不到1/4），文学和哲学的话题，脱离文本可能也着实难以分享
活动规模小，比较灵活，怎么样有节奏地摸着石头过河？是否该砍什么，加什么。
en: 'What Has Happened to This Group?': Review of the Year 2023
intro_en:
The Yanxia talk series held 41 sessions in 2023. Drawing on all the sessions and the feedback on them, this week we use our session time to look back and look ahead. What has the series become? In what direction will it go?
Content
Originality:
Many interesting niche topics rarely mentioned in the Chinese-speaking world: this is like excavation
Many topics widely discussed in other languages but missing from Chinese discourse: this is like translation
Some passionate, original talks drawing on speakers' own experiences: this is creation, but it can't be planned for
It feels like a history-and-geography set menu (32 sessions were related to history, 29 of them with a very clear regional focus). Many sessions followed the pattern of a story limited to a particular time and place, in the spirit of popular ideas such as microhistory and the citywalk.
Networked storytelling: different sessions echo and connect with one another. Speakers often say: "As we mentioned in our session on XX..."
Many Japan-related sessions (11 in total). This may reflect the great effort Japan has indeed made in history, culture and the arts.
Format
The session time can never satisfy everyone
The process for posting announcements has not been very rigorous
Publicity channels vary a lot
Balancing and managing talk time and discussion time
Realities and expectations worth discussing
A balance is needed between being informative/academic and being distinctive/entertaining
There may be a few too many Japan-related topics (about 11 sessions, a quarter of the total)
There really have been a lot of history topics (only 9 sessions were unrelated to history, less than a quarter); literature and philosophy topics are genuinely hard to present without the texts
The series is small and flexible; how do we keep a steady rhythm as we cross the river by feeling for the stones? Should we cut something, or add something?

zh: 北京为什么成了首都？
intro:
在漫长的中国历史中，北京从一个偏远的边疆城市慢慢发展成了全国的中心。北京在过去曾有哪些名字？是什么让北京完成了逆袭？它在地理上到底有什么得天独厚的条件？北京有没有真正的特产？它是不是一个吸血的城市？天下大乱的时候，哪些割据势力的大本营是北京？他们为什么都失败了？元、明、清、北洋和新中国为什么都把北京选作了都城？本期沙龙我们以这些问题为脉络，讲述北京这座城市的历史。

参考书目：侯仁之《北平历史地理》
en: Why Did Beijing Become the Capital?
intro_en:
Over China's long history, Beijing slowly grew from a remote frontier town into the centre of the whole country. What names has Beijing had in the past? What allowed Beijing to rise from underdog to capital? What natural geographical advantages does it actually have? Does Beijing have any genuine local specialities? Is it a city that bleeds the rest of the country dry? When the realm fell into chaos, which regional powers had their base in Beijing, and why did they all fail? Why did the Yuan, the Ming, the Qing, the Beiyang government and the People's Republic all choose Beijing as their capital? In this salon we use these questions as a thread to tell the history of the city of Beijing.

Reference: Hou Renzhi, An Historical Geography of Peiping

zh: 来者勿忘——上海罢工及五卅运动始末
intro:
- 本次分享上海的建立、发展、工业化，以及以五卅运动为代表的工人运动是如何发展的。
- 引起兴趣的问题：

    - 上海近代是如何逐步发展建立的
    - 上海的移民人口组成
    - 外国势力在上海的活动分布

    - 上海的工会运动和罢工发展
en: Lest We Forget: The Shanghai Strikes and the May Thirtieth Movement
intro_en:
- This session covers the founding, growth and industrialisation of Shanghai, and how the labour movement, epitomised by the May Thirtieth Movement, developed.
- Questions to spark interest:
    - Have you heard about the US auto workers' strike this September and October?
    - Who should be responsible for the losses caused by a strike?
    - How did Shanghai develop?
    - Why was modern Shanghai so important?
    - Why did the May Thirtieth Movement earn a place on the Monument to the People's Heroes?
- Questions for this session:
    - How modern Shanghai was built up step by step
    - The composition of Shanghai's migrant population
    - The distribution of foreign powers' activities in Shanghai
    - How party politics was conducted in Shanghai

zh: 从一贯道到郭继承——宗教习合在山东
intro:
在电影《我的1919》中，陈道明饰演的顾维钧面对巴黎和会上的各国代表时说："中国不能失去山东，就像西方不能失去耶路撒冷。"本次分享将以山东为主题，讨论各宗教在山东的发展历程。
注明：现实中顾维钧说的其实是“山东省是中华文明的摇篮，孔子和孟子的诞生地，对中国人而言，这是一块圣地。”
引起兴趣的问题：
宇宙万法的那个源头是什么？（？）
传统宗教和邪教的区别是什么？
为什么说：“中国不能失去山东，就像西方不能失去耶路撒冷”？
你还知道哪些综摄特色的宗教？
本次分享要讨论的问题：
各个宗教在山东发展的历程。
一贯道的出现、发展和现状。
最近互联网上一些和郭继承相关的梗。
怎么看待第三条道路？
en: From Yiguandao to Guo Jicheng: Syncretic Religion in Shandong
intro_en:
In the film My 1919, Chen Daoming, playing Wellington Koo, tells the delegates of the powers at the Paris Peace Conference: "China cannot lose Shandong, just as the West cannot lose Jerusalem." This session takes Shandong as its theme and looks at how the various religions developed there.
Note: what Wellington Koo actually said was, "The province of Shandong is the cradle of Chinese civilisation, the birthplace of Confucius and Mencius; for the Chinese it is a Holy Land."
Questions to get us thinking:
What is the source of all the dharmas of the universe? (?)
What is the difference between a traditional religion and a cult?
Why say that "China cannot lose Shandong, just as the West cannot lose Jerusalem"?
What other syncretic religions do you know of?
Questions for this session:
How the various religions developed in Shandong.
The emergence, development and present state of Yiguandao.
Some recent internet memes about Guo Jicheng.
What should we make of the "third way"?

zh: 五一六军事政变与首尔Citywalk
intro:
一些热场问题：

首尔旅行中印象较深的地方/希望去首尔看什么？

你对第二共和国和朴正熙有什么了解？

 “5.16军事政变”是1961年5月16日时任韩国陆军第二野战军副司令官朴正熙少将发动的一场军事政变。这次政变发生在四一九革命推翻李承晚政权后仅一年多之后，当时新成立的以张勉为内阁总理的民主党政权掌握了政治权力，但对社会的控制能力有限，且韩国的经济民生状况并未显著改善。

政变终结了短暂的“第二共和国”时期和民主党政府，同时促使朴正熙上台。这次政变中断了韩国的宪政秩序，开启了朴正熙长达18年的统治以及韩国32年的军人执政，同时也为韩国经济的腾飞创造了前提条件。

本次分享将讲述5.16军事政变的过程，介绍当时的各方势力，探讨政变的成功原因，并分享与5.16军事政变相关的首尔旅行“打卡地”。

准备讨论的问题：

当时韩国的政治势力：政治家（民主党新派/旧派）；军部；叛军；美军

政变经过

政变成功原因

首尔市内与5.16政变有关的旅游“打卡地”：

青瓦台（原朝鲜总督官邸）
世宗路建筑群： 原中央厅（日占原朝鲜总督府，已拆，现景福宫）、原国家再建最高会议厅舍（现韩国历史博物馆）、原国会议事堂（日占原京城府民馆、现首尔市议会）、德寿宫、原首尔市政府厅舍、原半岛酒店（已拆）
崇礼门
汉江大桥
国立首尔显忠院
en: The May 16 Coup and a Seoul City Walk
intro_en:
Some warm-up questions:

What places made the deepest impression on you when you travelled in Seoul, or what would you like to see there?

What do you know about the Second Republic and Park Chung-hee?

The May 16 coup was a military coup launched on 16 May 1961 by Major General Park Chung-hee, then deputy commander of the South Korean Army's Second Army. It came little more than a year after the April 19 Revolution had brought down Syngman Rhee's government. Political power was then in the hands of the newly formed Democratic Party government under Prime Minister Chang Myon, but its grip on society was weak, and the economy and people's livelihoods had not noticeably improved.

The coup ended the short-lived Second Republic and the Democratic Party government, and brought Park Chung-hee to power. It interrupted South Korea's constitutional order and began Park's eighteen years of rule and thirty-two years of military government in South Korea, while also laying the groundwork for the country's economic take-off.

This session will tell the story of the May 16 coup, introduce the forces involved at the time, explore why the coup succeeded, and share some Seoul sightseeing spots connected with it.

Questions we plan to discuss:

The political forces in South Korea at the time: the politicians (the new and old factions of the Democratic Party), the military, the rebel troops, and the US forces

How the coup unfolded

Why the coup succeeded

Sightseeing spots in Seoul connected with the May 16 coup:

The Blue House (formerly the residence of the Japanese Governor-General of Korea)
The buildings along Sejong-ro: the former Capitol (the Japanese Government-General Building, now demolished; the site is now part of Gyeongbokgung Palace), the former Supreme Council for National Reconstruction building (now the National Museum of Korean Contemporary History), the former National Assembly building (the Keijō Public Hall under Japanese rule, now the Seoul Metropolitan Council), Deoksugung Palace, the former Seoul City Hall, and the former Bando Hotel (now demolished)
Sungnyemun
Hangang Bridge
Seoul National Cemetery

zh: 当耶稣会遇见丰臣秀吉：日本的天主教世纪
intro:
1549年至1644年是日本吉利支丹（天主教徒）的世纪。而这段日本早期基督教历史和日本战国历史高度重合。耶稣会士带来了不光天主教信仰，还有西医和铁炮。日本战国时代西南诸多大名皈依了天主教，而丰臣秀吉的态度则经历了大逆转。天主教的传播也引发了后来的长崎教难、岛原之乱、德川锁国等等一系列对日本和东亚的历史产生了深远影响的事件。

1547年，西班牙耶稣会创始人方济各·沙勿略（Francis Xavier）在马六甲为一个叫 “安杰罗”(Anjiro)日本人施洗。正是这个我们所知的第一个日本基督徒把沙勿略带到了日本。
 
1578年，原本信仰禅宗的丰后国大名大友宗麟领洗成为天主教徒，并且在他的军队中以和欧洲十字军相同的十字架作为旗帜。也正是这一年，明智光秀的女儿玉子和天主教徒大名细川忠兴结婚。

细川玉子在1587年春天领洗成为天主教徒，同一年，大友宗麟去世，丰臣秀吉颁布“伴天连”（葡萄牙语Padre，即神父）禁令，驱逐天主教。

1596年，丰臣秀吉下令在京都和大坂逮捕了26名教士和信徒，并在翌年2月，以违背禁教令为名，将他们在长崎公开处死，掀开大迫害的序幕。

1600年，一艘荷兰商船登陆日本，船上的英国人威廉•亚当斯因给幕府造船有功，成为德川的外交顾问，并被封为武士，赐名“三浦按针”。亚当斯告诉德川，除了天主教外，基督教内还有新教，新教国家并不热衷传教，宗教和贸易也是脱钩的。而天主教国家往往通过传教来征服别国。

1637年，九州岛原地区的民众在天主教的旗帜下揭竿而起，发动江户时代最大规模的农民起义，最终被幕府镇压。

1644年，满清入关之年，在罗马加入耶稣会并获得神父职位的小西曼施欧（天主教大名小西行长的外孙）被捕殉教，自此日本再无神父，日本“天主教世纪”正式结束。同一时期，日本也开始了漫长的闭关锁国。

引起兴趣的分享点：

1. 在战国时代成为天主教徒并和耶稣会士及大名谈笑风生是怎样的体验？

2. 战国十字军是怎样的队伍？结局如何？

3. 在迫害酷刑下，日本战国时代的天主教徒都做出了哪些抉择？为什么有的人背教了而有的人没有？

准备和各位深入讨论的问题：

1. 天主教以及西班牙葡萄牙、新教以及荷兰等“南蛮”对日本战国历史产生了怎样的影响？

2. 长崎在日本历史上发挥的特殊作用？

3. 耶稣会的传教活动对东亚的历史产生了怎样的影响？

4.  天主教在中日韩的发展有何异同？

参考资料：雷立柏《日本教会史》笔记
五野井隆史《日本基督宗教史》
          马丁斯科塞斯电影《沉默》
          光荣出品游戏《太阁立志传5》
NHK纪录片《转动历史的时刻：战国十字军》
en: When the Jesuits Met Toyotomi Hideyoshi: Japan's Christian Century
intro_en:
The years 1549 to 1644 were the century of Japan's Kirishitan, its Catholics. This early chapter of Christianity in Japan overlaps closely with the Sengoku period. The Jesuits brought not only the Catholic faith but also Western medicine and firearms. Many daimyō in south-western Japan converted to Catholicism during the Sengoku period, while Toyotomi Hideyoshi's attitude went through a dramatic reversal. The spread of Catholicism also set off a chain of events, including the Nagasaki persecutions, the Shimabara Rebellion and the Tokugawa policy of national seclusion, that had a profound effect on the history of Japan and East Asia.

In 1547, Francis Xavier, the Spanish co-founder of the Society of Jesus, baptised a Japanese man named Anjirō in Malacca. It was this man, the first Japanese Christian we know of, who brought Xavier to Japan.

In 1578, Ōtomo Sōrin, daimyō of Bungo Province and formerly a follower of Zen, was baptised a Catholic, and his army carried a cross as its banner, just like the European crusaders. In the same year, Akechi Mitsuhide's daughter Tama married the Catholic daimyō Hosokawa Tadaoki.

Hosokawa Tama was baptised a Catholic in the spring of 1587. That same year Ōtomo Sōrin died, and Toyotomi Hideyoshi issued his edict against the bateren (from the Portuguese padre, "father", meaning priests), expelling the Catholic missionaries.

In 1596, Hideyoshi ordered the arrest of twenty-six priests and believers in Kyoto and Osaka, and in February of the following year they were publicly executed in Nagasaki for violating the ban on the faith, marking the start of the great persecution.

In 1600, a Dutch merchant ship reached Japan. On board was an Englishman, William Adams, who, having built ships for the shogunate, became a diplomatic adviser to Tokugawa, was made a samurai and given the name Miura Anjin. Adams told Tokugawa that besides Catholicism, Christianity also included Protestantism; Protestant countries were not keen on missionary work, and for them religion and trade were separate, whereas Catholic countries often used missionary work as a means of conquering other lands.

In 1637, the people of Shimabara in Kyushu rose up under the banner of Catholicism in the largest peasant revolt of the Edo period, which was eventually crushed by the shogunate.

In 1644, the year the Manchu Qing entered China through the passes, Konishi Mancio (grandson of the Catholic daimyō Konishi Yukinaga), who had joined the Jesuits and been ordained a priest in Rome, was arrested and martyred. From then on there were no more priests in Japan, and Japan's "Christian century" formally came to an end. In the same period, Japan also entered its long era of seclusion.

Points of interest:

1. What was it like to become a Catholic in the Sengoku period and chat and joke with Jesuits and daimyō?

2. What kind of force were the Sengoku crusaders, and what became of them?

3. Under persecution and torture, what choices did Japan's Sengoku-era Catholics make? Why did some renounce their faith while others did not?

Questions we'd like to discuss in depth:

1. What influence did Catholicism and Spain and Portugal, and Protestantism and the Netherlands, the so-called "southern barbarians", have on the history of Sengoku Japan?

2. What special role has Nagasaki played in Japanese history?

3. How did the Jesuits' missionary work affect the history of East Asia?

4. How did the development of Catholicism in China, Japan and Korea compare?

References: notes on Leopold Leeb's History of the Church in Japan
Gonoi Takashi, A History of Christianity in Japan
Martin Scorsese's film Silence
Koei's game Taikō Risshiden V
NHK documentary The Moment History Turned: The Sengoku Crusaders

zh: 孽海花——晚清变局中的风流与政治
intro:
鲁迅在《中国小说史略》中将《孽海花》举为晚清四大谴责小说，评价其“结构工巧，文采斐然“。《孽海花》以真人真事为影射，所牵扯人物有名士名妓，达官大吏，也有仆从小厮，甚至清朝皇帝、欧洲王室、日本浪人、八国联军司令，是以当时上层知识分子的视角，写风流韵事，八卦掌故，更写历史更迭，政治脉络的一部奇书。


将要讨论的问题：

几段风流韵事与官场政治：
才子与王妃
名士与名妓
将军与苗女
清流与闺秀
傀儡皇帝与知己宠妃。

遗老争传《清夜录》——张爱玲的证言。

引起兴趣的话题：

写出“不拘一格降人才”的龚自珍的儿子何以成为第一个“带路党”？
名妓赛金花与八国联军司令瓦德西一段情缘救中国？
宫斗剧、武侠小说、戏说传奇中常见情节之鼻祖？
en: A Flower in a Sinful Sea: Romance and Politics in the Late Qing
intro_en:
In his A Brief History of Chinese Fiction, Lu Xun counted A Flower in a Sinful Sea among the four great novels of exposure of the late Qing, praising it as "ingeniously constructed and brilliantly written". The novel is a roman à clef built on real people and events. Its cast includes famous scholars and celebrated courtesans, high officials and great ministers, servants and pageboys, and even the Qing emperor, European royalty, Japanese rōnin and the commander of the Eight-Nation Alliance. Written from the point of view of the upper-class intellectuals of the day, it is a remarkable book that records love affairs, gossip and anecdotes, and above all the turning of history and the currents of politics.

Questions for discussion:

Several love affairs and the politics of officialdom:
The talented scholar and the princess
The famous scholar and the famous courtesan
The general and the Miao girl
The Qingliu official and the young lady of good family
The puppet emperor and his beloved consort and confidante.

The old Qing loyalists vie to pass around the Qingye lu: Eileen Chang's testimony.

Topics of interest:

How did the son of Gong Zizhen, who wrote "choose talent without regard to convention", become the first man to guide a foreign invader?
Did the famous courtesan Sai Jinhua save China through her romance with Waldersee, commander of the Eight-Nation Alliance?
Is this the ancestor of plot devices common in palace-intrigue dramas, martial arts novels and fanciful historical romances?

zh: 因为想篡位只好让老板建国了
intro:
五代十国期间，在江淮和江西地区曾经先后建立过两个相互承接，版图相似的政权，杨吴和南唐。在五代十国的战乱中，这两个政权控制的区域内保持了较长时间的和平和繁荣，文化和经济逐渐赶上了一直领先了上千年的北方。

然而，崛起于黄巢之乱的背景下，杨吴政权的前身——杨行密下辖的淮南军并不比同时代其他的军阀政权更加“文明”和内敛，反而一直是南方地区最咄咄逼人的势力。然而连续的继承危机逐渐改变了这个集团的色彩，也影响了整个南方地区的政治局面。

通过这一期活动，通过叙述徐温和徐知诰两代杨吴权臣的一些故事，梳理杨吴和平转变成南唐的过程，我们可以稍微了解一下这两个政权截然不同的底色，并且勾勒出一条晚唐五代时期军阀政权的转型出路。

一些可以热场讨论的问题：

从武德爆炸的晚唐走向重文轻武的北宋，中间发生过一些什么样的变化？

东南地区为何能在战乱频繁的五代十国期间保持相对的和平和繁荣？

你能想到历史上的哪些“傀儡政权”？

活动结束后我们还可以试着讨论以下的一些问题：

怎么看待徐温和徐知诰保境安民的选择？

杨吴到南唐的嬗变，是北宋政治的一面镜子吗？

两宋时期对杨吴-南唐政权的评价为什么越来越好？
en: Wanting the Throne, He Had to Make the Boss Found a State
intro_en:
During the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period, two successive regimes with similar territories were established in the Jianghuai region and Jiangxi: Yang Wu and the Southern Tang. Amid the wars of the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms, the lands they controlled enjoyed a fairly long stretch of peace and prosperity, and their culture and economy gradually caught up with the north, which had led the way for more than a thousand years.

Yet the forerunner of the Yang Wu regime, the Huainan army under Yang Xingmi, which rose amid the Huang Chao rebellion, was no more "civilised" or restrained than the other warlord regimes of its day; on the contrary, it was always the most aggressive power in the south. A series of succession crises, however, gradually changed the character of this group, and also shaped the political situation of the whole south.

In this session, through stories of Xu Wen and Xu Zhigao, two generations of powerful ministers of Yang Wu, we will trace how Yang Wu was peacefully transformed into the Southern Tang. Along the way we can get a sense of the very different underlying character of the two regimes, and sketch one way out that was open to warlord regimes of the late Tang and Five Dynasties.

Some warm-up questions:

What changed between the late Tang, bursting with martial energy, and the Northern Song, which prized civil over military?

Why was the south-east able to stay relatively peaceful and prosperous through the frequent wars of the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms?

What "puppet regimes" in history can you think of?

After the session we can also try to discuss the following questions:

What should we make of Xu Wen and Xu Zhigao's choice to protect their territory and keep the people safe?

Is the transformation from Yang Wu to the Southern Tang a mirror of Northern Song politics?

Why did assessments of the Yang Wu and Southern Tang regimes grow more and more favourable during the Song?

zh: 硅谷Citywalk：从世界果园到ChatGPT
intro:
之前我们介绍过截止到二战前后的旧金山历史，这次我们继续上次的话题，以“硅谷”为中心看看这片土地二战后发生了什么，是怎么从一片大农村发展成现在这个科技创新中心的？这些历史又是怎样塑造了现在硅谷地区的企业/地区文化还有什么样的影响？

- 为什么湾区人民喜欢摘樱桃/摘草莓？
- 硅谷的崛起和斯坦福大学/伯克利大学关系很大么？
- 硅谷为什么叫“硅”谷？为什么好像都是台积电在造芯片而不是硅谷的大公司？台积电和硅谷什么关系？
- 你听说过和曾经和IBM打擂台的王安电脑公司么？为什么历史上那么多公司都快速崛起快速倒闭了？
- 为什么硅谷现在人人想创业？
- 现在去哪儿能看到实际意义上的硅谷？
- 风险投资对硅谷的崛起真的有很大帮助么？
- 如果给整个硅谷地区选一个市长（Mayor），谁最实至名归？
- 为什么不是波士顿地区/西雅图地区/达拉斯地区成为“硅谷”？
en: A Silicon Valley City Walk: From the World's Orchard to ChatGPT
intro_en:
Last time we covered the history of San Francisco up to around the Second World War. This time we pick up where we left off and, with Silicon Valley at the centre, look at what happened to this land after the war. How did it grow from a big stretch of farmland into today's hub of technological innovation? And how has this history shaped the corporate and regional culture of the Silicon Valley area today, and what other effects has it had?

- Why do people in the Bay Area love picking cherries and strawberries?
- Did Stanford and Berkeley have much to do with the rise of Silicon Valley?
- Why is Silicon Valley called "Silicon" Valley? Why does it seem that TSMC makes the chips rather than the big Silicon Valley companies? What is TSMC's relationship with Silicon Valley?
- Have you heard of Wang Laboratories, the computer company that once went head to head with IBM? Why have so many companies in its history risen quickly and collapsed just as quickly?
- Why does everyone in Silicon Valley want to start a company these days?
- Where can you go today to see Silicon Valley in the literal sense?
- Did venture capital really help much in the rise of Silicon Valley?
- If the whole Silicon Valley area were to choose a mayor, who would most deserve the title?
- Why did Boston, Seattle or Dallas not become "Silicon Valley"?

zh: 本意是好的
intro:
很多失败的国家项目结束后，我们经常能听到这种感叹：“本意是好的，只是下面执行错了。”然而事实真的是这样吗？这一次，我们会分享詹姆斯·C·斯科特的《国家的视角》，谈一谈那些失败的国家项目。这些轰轰烈烈的运动是如何发起的？为什么他们后来都失败了？

你看过马前卒的“睡前消息”吗？马前卒提出了很多雄心勃勃的建议：比如社会化抚养、消灭小农经济、全面普及儿童手环……你同意这些建议吗？反对的理由又是什么？

在参加下次分享之前，我强烈推荐两个有趣的资源：

小约翰可汗的视频“英国如何给非洲人民送福利？【神奇组织08】”：https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1uk4y1u7aY/

豆子的微小说“改粮为桑”：https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/33174367
en: Good Intentions
intro_en:
After many failed state projects come to an end, we often hear the lament: "The intentions were good; it was just carried out badly further down." But is that really so? This time we will share James C. Scott's Seeing Like a State and talk about failed state projects. How were these grand, sweeping campaigns launched? And why did they all end in failure?

Have you watched Ma Qianzu's "Bedtime News"? Ma Qianzu has put forward many ambitious proposals, such as socialised child-rearing, eliminating the smallholder economy, and universal wristbands for children. Do you agree with these proposals? And if not, what are your reasons?

Before coming to the next session, I strongly recommend two interesting resources:

Little John Khan's video "How Britain Delivered Welfare to the People of Africa [Amazing Organisations 08]": https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1uk4y1u7aY/

Douzi's micro-story "Replacing Grain with Mulberry": https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/33174367

zh: 动漫地理学102：《孤独摇滚！》 下北泽！
intro:
本次分享介绍动漫《孤独摇滚！》，介绍其中社恐相关的话题，介绍故事发生地下北泽的故事。

引起兴趣的问题：
你看过《孤独摇滚！》吗？
社恐是天生的吗？
下北泽为何成为（亚）文化胜地的？
野兽先辈到底是什么梗？
本次分享将讨论的内容：
《孤独摇滚！》讲了一个什么故事？
社恐在《孤独摇滚！》中有哪些细节体现？
社恐是否是一个心理问题？如果是该如何解决？
下北泽是一个什么样的地方？
Disclaimer：
对于无法理解社恐的人，这部动漫在社恐的描绘上似乎有些无法理解。如果对社恐概念无法接受，请谨慎选择是否需要参与。

Reference：
孤独摇滚！
《孤独摇滚！》舞台剧
en: Anime Geography 102: Bocchi the Rock! and Shimokitazawa
intro_en:
This session introduces the anime Bocchi the Rock!, the topics it raises around social anxiety, and the story of Shimokitazawa, where it is set.

Questions to get us thinking:
Have you seen Bocchi the Rock!?
Is social anxiety innate?
How did Shimokitazawa become a mecca of (sub)culture?
What exactly is the "Yajū Senpai" meme?
What this session will discuss:
What story does Bocchi the Rock! tell?
In what details does social anxiety show up in Bocchi the Rock!?
Is social anxiety a psychological problem? If so, how can it be dealt with?
What kind of place is Shimokitazawa?
Disclaimer:
For people who cannot relate to social anxiety, the anime's portrayal of it may seem somewhat hard to understand. If you find the idea of social anxiety hard to accept, please think carefully about whether to attend.

References:
Bocchi the Rock!
Bocchi the Rock! stage play

zh: 动漫地理学101：镰仓——何为真物
intro:
本次分享将讲述与日本镰仓相关的历史故事和影视作品，探究千百年来这座城市的变迁。

引起兴趣的问题：
你是否听说过镰仓这个城市？
你是否听说过镰仓幕府，或者镰仓的历史？
镰仓有哪些好玩的地方？
你是否听说过《我的青春恋爱物语果然有问题。》？
你是否听说过……算了如果你感兴趣就搜搜吧！

将要讨论的问题：
镰仓幕府的兴亡。
佛教曹洞宗、临济宗、净土宗、日莲宗分别有什么区别？
《春物》到底讲了一个什么样的故事？
为什么有很多文学家，诸如芥川、川端等人，选择了在镰仓居住？
有哪些跟镰仓相关的影视作品？

《晚春》（电影）
en: Anime Geography 101: Kamakura and What Is Real
intro_en:
This session will tell historical stories and look at films and series connected with Kamakura in Japan, exploring how the city has changed over the centuries.

Questions to get us thinking:
Have you heard of the city of Kamakura?
Have you heard of the Kamakura shogunate, or of Kamakura's history?
What fun places are there in Kamakura?
Have you heard of My Youth Romantic Comedy Is Wrong, As I Expected?
Have you heard of... never mind, if you're interested, look it up!

Questions for discussion:
The rise and fall of the Kamakura shogunate.
What are the differences between the Sōtō, Rinzai, Jōdo and Nichiren schools of Buddhism?
What story does Oregairu actually tell?
Why did so many writers, such as Akutagawa and Kawabata, choose to live in Kamakura?
What films and series are connected with Kamakura?

Late Spring (film)

zh: 松都明月——开京与黄真伊
intro:
本次分享朝鲜妓生黄真伊的生平、诗作，以及其故乡开城的历史。

引起兴趣的问题：
朝鲜的历史是怎么发展的？如何演变成今天的局面？
你还了解哪些妓生（歌妓，艺妓）的故事？
汉语文化圈在历史上对周边国家造成了什么影响？
将讨论的问题：
黄真伊的生平有哪些故事？她有哪些出名的作品？
开城是如何一步步发展到今天的样子？
如何看待韩国人对于黄真伊的影视作品改编？以及中国网友以《梦华录》做对比？
en: The Bright Moon of Songdo: Kaegyŏng and Hwang Jini
intro_en:
This session covers the life and poetry of the Joseon gisaeng Hwang Jini, and the history of her home town, Kaesong.

Questions to get us thinking:
How did Korean history unfold, and how did it arrive at today's situation?
What other stories of gisaeng (singing girls, courtesans) do you know?
What influence has the Sinosphere had on neighbouring countries through history?
Questions for discussion:
What stories are there from Hwang Jini's life? What are her best-known works?
How did Kaesong develop, step by step, into what it is today?
What should we make of South Korean film and television adaptations of Hwang Jini's life, and of Chinese netizens comparing them with Dream of Splendor?

zh: 遮莫先驱到望舒
intro:
中秋节是中国最重要的传统节日之一。每年中秋，嫦娥奔月、吴刚伐桂、玉兔捣药的故事，无数诗词歌赋和各式月饼就会营造出浓浓的节日氛围。然而，如果我们以更深更广的世界视角来看待中秋神话故事，是否能发现更多以前从未注意到奇妙情节和深层意蕴？

本次分享将由比较中国嫦娥奔月故事和西方阿波罗与达芙妮的故事说起，探讨古代神话共通的天文学含义和跨越东西方的生命旅程经验，看看东西方对于月亮、宇宙、长生、永恒各自留下了怎样的深刻见解，以及中国人眼中的月亮到底有何特别。

拟讨论的问题：

夜光何德，死则又育？
厥利维何，而顾菟(tù)在腹？
--屈原 楚辞 天问

月亮在中国古典传统中到底有多少雅称？有哪些雅称背后暗含深意？

嫦娥奔月究竟是为了啥？

吴刚犯了什么罪，为啥受到这种形式的惩罚？

白兔捣药捣的啥药？

月亮上的桂树有何特别？

中国人对月亮有何特别的见解？这些见解从哪里来的？
en: Let the Moon Lead the Way
intro_en:
The Mid-Autumn Festival is one of China's most important traditional festivals. Every year at Mid-Autumn, the stories of Chang'e flying to the moon, Wu Gang felling the osmanthus tree and the Jade Rabbit pounding medicine, along with countless poems and all kinds of mooncakes, create a rich festive atmosphere. But if we look at the Mid-Autumn myths from a deeper and broader, global perspective, can we find wonderful details and deeper meanings we had never noticed before?

This session begins by comparing the Chinese story of Chang'e flying to the moon with the Western story of Apollo and Daphne. It explores the astronomical meanings shared by ancient myths and the experience of life's journey that spans East and West, looks at the profound insights East and West each left us about the moon, the cosmos, longevity and eternity, and asks what is really so special about the moon in Chinese eyes.

Questions we plan to discuss:

What virtue has the light of night, that it dies and then is born again?
What does it gain, that it keeps the hare (gutu) in its belly?
-- Qu Yuan, Chu Ci, "Heavenly Questions"

How many elegant names does the moon have in the Chinese classical tradition? Which of them carry hidden meanings?

Why exactly did Chang'e fly to the moon?

What crime did Wu Gang commit, and why was he punished in this particular way?

What medicine is the white rabbit pounding?

What is special about the osmanthus tree on the moon?

What particular views of the moon do the Chinese hold? Where do these views come from?

zh: 日本浮世绘的正面与侧面
intro:
说到日本文化，浮世绘是无法避开的一个主题，甚至可以说大部分日本文化符号的传播和推广都离不开相关的浮世绘作品。本期活动我们就来走近浮世绘，看看它到底是什么东西，怎么发展成我们熟悉的这个形式的，以及有哪些重要画家和作品，我们也会讨论到浮世绘这个话题里一些不为人所熟知的细节和小故事。



一些值得思考的问题：

浮世绘为什么会在江户幕府时期产生并且迅速流行？

一张浮世绘在当时值多少钱？现在又值多少钱？

为什么浮世绘里这么多春画？

如何分辨浮世绘里出现各种人物（艺伎，游女，武士）？

为什么会有那种整个画面就是一个头的作品？

葛饰北斋和歌川广重谁更牛？

没有浮世绘就不会有印象派和德彪西么？

为什么『神奈川冲浪里』能火遍全球？
en: Ukiyo-e: Front and Profile
intro_en:
There is no avoiding ukiyo-e when it comes to Japanese culture; one could even say that most of the symbols of Japanese culture owe their spread and popularity to ukiyo-e works. In this session we take a closer look at ukiyo-e: what exactly it is, how it developed into the form we know, and who its important artists and works are. We will also talk about some little-known details and stories on the subject.

Some questions worth thinking about:

Why did ukiyo-e emerge and quickly become popular during the Edo shogunate?

How much was a ukiyo-e print worth back then? And how much is it worth now?

Why are there so many shunga (erotic pictures) among ukiyo-e?

How can you tell apart the various figures (geisha, courtesans, samurai) who appear in ukiyo-e?

Why are there works in which the whole picture is just one head?

Who was greater, Katsushika Hokusai or Utagawa Hiroshige?

Without ukiyo-e, would there have been no Impressionism and no Debussy?

Why did The Great Wave off Kanagawa become famous all over the world?

zh: 甲申诗史--吴梅村书写的一六四四
intro:
吴伟业，字骏公，号梅村，是明清之际著名诗人，他于长篇歌行上的造诣，与元（稹）白（居易）的长庆体齐名；名列“江左三大家”，却也被列入乾隆年间修订的贰臣传。他一生曲折经历造就了其冠绝一时的诗艺，更因历经两朝的“亡国之人，血心流注”倾注出诗史之笔。


本次分享将由吴梅村围绕甲申之变的长篇歌行，试一窥王朝易代之际从皇族到平民各阶层的哀乐境遇，及诗歌中“推见至隐”的历史细节。


引起兴趣的问题：

梅村笔下崇祯与田贵妃，吴三桂与陈圆圆，冒辟疆与董小宛，他自己与卞玉京的风流韵事

清初三大疑案之世祖出家，在梅村诗中或有线索？

最近冒出红楼梦作者为吴梅村的言论，尊嘟假嘟？


讨论的问题：

何为诗史互证？

吴梅村笔下的明末情景

亡国之叹中的人性维度
en: A Poet's History of 1644: Wu Meicun
intro_en:
Wu Weiye, courtesy name Jungong, sobriquet Meicun, was a celebrated poet of the Ming–Qing transition. His mastery of the long song-form ballad is ranked alongside the Changqing style of Yuan Zhen and Bai Juyi. He was counted among the "Three Masters of Jiangzuo", yet was also listed in the Biographies of Twice-Serving Officials compiled under the Qianlong emperor. The twists and turns of his life shaped a poetic art unrivalled in his day, and as "a man whose country had perished, pouring out his heart's blood" across two dynasties, he wrote with the pen of a poet-historian.

This session will use Wu Meicun's long ballads on the upheaval of 1644 to glimpse the joys and sorrows of every level of society, from the imperial family to commoners, at the change of dynasties, and the historical details that his poems "infer from the visible to the hidden".

Questions to get us thinking:

The love affairs in Meicun's poems: the Chongzhen emperor and Consort Tian, Wu Sangui and Chen Yuanyuan, Mao Pijiang and Dong Xiaowan, and Meicun himself and Bian Yujing

Might Meicun's poems hold clues to one of the three great mysteries of the early Qing, the Shunzhi emperor becoming a monk?

Recently the claim has surfaced that Wu Meicun was the author of Dream of the Red Chamber. For real, or not for real?

Questions for discussion:

What is the mutual verification of poetry and history?

Wu Meicun's depiction of the late Ming

The human dimension in laments for a fallen dynasty

zh: 能文能武皇甫晖
intro:
本次分享将从有名小卒皇甫晖的视角，揭开五代十国时期的一些社会风貌。

一些引起兴趣的问题：
唐代末年的混乱是如何愈演愈烈的？
五代十国有哪些国家？
有哪些让人耳熟能详的故事？
本次分享将讨论的问题：
皇甫晖是谁？
邺都之变和兴教门之变是怎么发生的？
后唐真的是亡于伶人吗？李存勗、李嗣源和魏博军的关系怎么样？
皇甫晖前往南唐的途中经历过什么奇妙冒险？
en: Huangfu Hui, Scholar and Soldier
intro_en:
This session looks at society in the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period through the eyes of Huangfu Hui, a "famous nobody".

Some questions to get us thinking:
How did the chaos at the end of the Tang grow ever worse?
Which states made up the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms?
What well-known stories are there from the period?
Questions for this session:
Who was Huangfu Hui?
How did the Yedu mutiny and the Xingjiao Gate incident come about?
Did the Later Tang really fall because of actors? What was the relationship between Li Cunxu, Li Siyuan and the Weibo army?
What strange adventures did Huangfu Hui have on his way to the Southern Tang?

zh: 斜阳与铁：昭和中期文学一瞥
intro:
我把自我当做房屋时，我的肉体就仿佛围绕着这座房屋的果园……

我开始拼命地耕耘这片果园，为我所用的就是太阳与铁。”

——《太阳与铁》，三岛由纪夫

二十世纪初，统称“华族”的日本旧贵族以哼歌般的轻快速度衰落了下去，直至二战结束两年后彻底被废除；牺牲封建贵族得来的天皇集权在军国主义中衰退，直至他用前所未有的几次亲声广播正式取消了自己的神格、从国民身份中剥离了神道信仰；而军国主义本身则屈服于美军的强大武力，使大日本帝国降格为了日本国。这一切事件和一百多年来进入的多种西方思想与文化一起，将一代人的精神从政教合一的“八纮一宇”沙文主义又一次导向了全新的方向；而在文化前线和经济顶点的文人自然受到了最大的冲击，连或隐或显地传承着的古典美学也慢慢失却。我们将对这悬日低垂时代的两人作短暂一瞥。太宰治：代表作《人间失格》。他是小村议员之家的六男，入赘的父亲于二十世纪刚得贵族地位，华族制度却快速消失了。颓废的那部分的作品中主角常自卑地无以存在，却也常以“粗鄙”贬低世人。38岁第五次自杀终获成功，遗留下未完成的喜剧《Goodbye》。

三岛由纪夫：成名作《假面的自白》。自我标榜为太宰的宿敌，无法忍受其“少年乡巴佬的野心”。他的祖母有德川家的遥远血统，曾在亲王宫中学习礼仪，自身作为长男一直处于其严密监护之下，亦在其坚持下自小就读贵族学习院。他的性取向仍有争议，但其对自身理想中健美肉体的狂热有目共睹。


希望各位在参与前能选择阅读这篇故友所作的的知乎短答：

日本文化中「侘寂、幽玄、物哀」三者有何区别？
