en: Setting Sun and Iron: A Glimpse of Mid-Shōwa Literature
intro_en:
"When I regarded my self as a house, my body was like an orchard surrounding it...

I set about cultivating this orchard with all my might, and what I used for it was the sun and iron."

-- Mishima Yukio, Sun and Steel

In the early twentieth century, Japan's old nobility, known collectively as the kazoku, declined with the light, carefree speed of a hummed tune, until they were abolished altogether two years after the end of the Second World War. The imperial centralisation won at the expense of the feudal nobility withered under militarism, until the emperor, in a few unprecedented broadcasts in his own voice, formally renounced his divinity and stripped Shinto belief from national identity. Militarism itself yielded to the overwhelming force of the US military, and the Empire of Great Japan was demoted to the State of Japan. All these events, together with the many Western ideas and cultures that had entered Japan over more than a century, once again turned the spirit of a generation away from the chauvinism of hakkō ichiu, with its union of state and religion, towards an entirely new direction. Writers on the cultural front line and at the economic peak naturally felt the greatest impact, and even the classical aesthetics that had been handed down, sometimes hidden and sometimes plain, gradually slipped away. We will take a brief look at two men of this age of the low-hanging sun. Dazai Osamu: best known for No Longer Human. He was the sixth son of a village assemblyman's family; his father, who had married into the family, gained noble status only at the start of the twentieth century, but the kazoku system soon disappeared. In his decadent works the protagonists often feel so inferior that they can barely exist, yet they also often disparage the world as "vulgar". At thirty-eight, on his fifth suicide attempt, he finally succeeded, leaving behind the unfinished comedy Goodbye.

Mishima Yukio: made his name with Confessions of a Mask. He styled himself Dazai's archrival and could not stand Dazai's "country-bumpkin, adolescent ambition". His grandmother had a distant blood tie to the Tokugawa family and had learned etiquette at the household of an imperial prince; as the eldest son, Mishima was kept under her close watch, and at her insistence he attended the Gakushūin, the Peers' School, from childhood. His sexual orientation is still debated, but his fanatical devotion to his ideal of a strong, beautiful body is plain for all to see.

Before attending, we hope you will read this short Zhihu answer by an old friend:

What is the difference between wabi-sabi, yūgen and mono no aware in Japanese culture?

https://www.zhihu.com/question/24982618/answer/120953016

zh: “我太想进步了”——南京古都身份构建的历程
intro:
一些可以热场讨论的问题：
关于南京，你知道它有哪些其他的名字？
南京曾经担任过哪些政权的政治中心？
秦汉时代的南方，出现过哪些值得一提的城市？南京在当时叫做什么？



中国的几大著名古都几乎都坐落于关中和华北平原的区域，而南京是唯一一个位于长江流域的例外。虽然担任全国性政权的首都的时间不长，但是顶着“六朝古都”的名声，南京几乎是历史上长江中下游地区无可争议的政治中心。

为此，许多人曾经从各种角度论证南京作为一座首都的各项有利条件。

然而，通过这一期活动，我们也许会发现这一切并非那么理所应当。

在秦汉时期几乎默默无闻的南京，是在三国时期突然超越了一众南方大城市，成为了东吴的国都。而在此后的数百年中，南京的地位一直在争议中起伏，却又在种种机缘下不断的加强，并终于在南朝的末期彻底完成了一座古都恢弘的构建过程。历时将近三百年，南京才真正成为了中国南方无可争议政治中心。

我们将把重点放在公元4-5世纪的时局变动和人文心态上，梳理南京构建古都地位的过程和其中的标志性事件。



活动结束后我们还可以试着讨论以下的一些问题：
未能长期担任全国性首都的南京，是一座偏安之都么？
对于一个政权来说，大建宫室意味着什么？
南宋是出于什么原因放弃了定都南京？
en: 'I Really Want to Get Ahead': How Nanjing Built Its Identity as an Ancient Capital
intro_en:
Some warm-up questions:
What other names for Nanjing do you know?
Which regimes has Nanjing served as the political centre of?
What notable cities were there in the south during the Qin and Han? What was Nanjing called then?

China's great ancient capitals are almost all in the Guanzhong region and the North China Plain; Nanjing is the only exception in the Yangtze basin. Although it was not the capital of a nationwide regime for long, Nanjing, with its reputation as "ancient capital of the Six Dynasties", was for most of history the undisputed political centre of the middle and lower Yangtze.

For this reason, many people have argued from all sorts of angles for Nanjing's advantages as a capital.

Through this session, however, we may discover that none of this was so self-evident.

Nanjing, almost unknown in the Qin and Han, suddenly overtook the other great cities of the south in the Three Kingdoms period to become the capital of Eastern Wu. Over the following centuries its status rose and fell amid controversy, yet kept being strengthened by one turn of events after another, until at the end of the Southern Dynasties it finally completed its grand construction as an ancient capital. It took nearly three hundred years for Nanjing truly to become the undisputed political centre of southern China.

We will focus on the political changes and the intellectual and cultural mood of the fourth and fifth centuries AD, tracing how Nanjing built its status as an ancient capital and the landmark events along the way.

After the session we can also try to discuss the following questions:
Was Nanjing, which never served long as a national capital, a capital of a regime content with ruling half the country?
What does building grand palaces mean for a regime?
Why did the Southern Song decide against making Nanjing its capital?

zh: 汉奸三部曲——“我为其难”汪兆铭
intro:
本次分享将以汪兆铭的文学作品为线索，分享和讨论他在不同时期的性格以及做出决策的心态。

引起兴趣的问题：
什么是汉奸？定义是什么？
汪精卫有哪些文学作品？
汪精卫的人生轨迹经历过哪些变化？
汪精卫的性格有哪些特色？
你知道汪精卫的什么故事？
将要讨论的问题：
汪精卫的生平有哪些经历？
如何看待汪精卫的文学作品和政治行为？
如何看待国民党左右派斗争和四一二事件？
汪精卫为什么选择与日本人合作？
一些文学人士对汪精卫的诗评：

题某氏集 钱钟书
扫叶吞花足胜情，钜公难得此才清。
微嫌东野殊寒相，似觉南风有死声。
孟德月明忧有绝，元衡日出事还生。
莫将愁苦求诗好，高位从来谶易成。

阜昌 陈寅恪
阜昌天子赋能诗，集选中州未肯遗。
阮瑀多才原不忝，褚渊迟死更堪悲。
千秋读史心难论，一局收枰胜属谁。
事变无穷东海涸，冤禽公案有传疑。

无题 叶嘉莹
曾将薪釜喻初襟，举世凭谁证此心。
未择高原桑枉植，怜他千古作冤禽。
en: The Collaborators, Part One: Wang Jingwei, 'Doing the Hard Thing'
intro_en:
This session follows the thread of Wang Zhaoming's literary works to share and discuss his character at different periods and his state of mind as he made his decisions.

Questions to get us thinking:
What is a hanjian, a traitor to China? How is it defined?
What literary works did Wang Jingwei write?
What changes did Wang Jingwei's life go through?
What were the distinctive features of Wang Jingwei's character?
What stories about Wang Jingwei do you know?
Questions for discussion:
What did Wang Jingwei experience in his life?
How should we view Wang Jingwei's literary works and his political actions?
How should we view the struggle between the left and right wings of the Kuomintang, and the April 12 Incident?
Why did Wang Jingwei choose to collaborate with the Japanese?
Some literary figures' poems on Wang Jingwei:

"Inscribed on a Certain Gentleman's Collection" by Qian Zhongshu
Sweeping leaves and swallowing blossoms, his feeling is fine enough; rare in a great lord is talent so pure.
Yet I faintly mind that, like Dongye, he has a strangely wintry air, and seem to hear the sound of death in the southern wind.
Mengde, under the bright moon, grieved that his cares might end; for Yuanheng, at sunrise, trouble arose once more.
Do not seek fine poems through sorrow and bitterness: for those in high places, omens have always been quick to come true.

"Fuchang" by Chen Yinke
The Fuchang Son of Heaven could write poems; the anthology of the Central Plains would not leave him out.
Ruan Yu's many talents were no disgrace to him; Chu Yuan, dying too late, is sadder still.
Reading history a thousand autumns on, the heart is hard to judge; when the game is cleared from the board, whose is the victory?
Endless are the changes, till the Eastern Sea runs dry; the case of the wronged bird is still handed down in doubt.

"Untitled" by Ye Jiaying
Once he likened his first resolve to the firewood and the cauldron; in all the world, who can bear witness to this heart?
Not choosing high ground, the mulberry was planted in vain; I pity him, a wronged bird for all time.

zh: 嵇康《琴賦》
intro:
本次分享來自於太玄琴社社長，九歌詩社社員錢力。借由對琴賦的賞析，管窺嵇康的人文思想，簡單介紹古琴與雅樂，進而與大家一起探索琴詩之道。


引起興趣的問題：
鐵匠？詩人？琴師？嵇康者誰？
為什麼說『琴乃眾器之首』?
廣陵散為何沒有失傳？

將會探討的問題：
琴賦的思想內涵為何？
人可以通過音樂得道嗎？
嵇康之死是必然的嗎？
en: Xi Kang's Rhapsody on the Qin
intro_en:
This session is given by Qian Li, president of the Taixuan Qin Society and a member of the Jiuge Poetry Society. Through an appreciation of the "Rhapsody on the Qin", we will glimpse Xi Kang's humanistic thought, give a brief introduction to the guqin and ritual court music, and explore together the way of the qin and poetry.

Questions to get us thinking:
Blacksmith? Poet? Qin player? Who was Xi Kang?
Why is it said that "the qin is the foremost of all instruments"?
Why was Guangling San not lost?

Questions we will explore:
What are the ideas behind the "Rhapsody on the Qin"?
Can one attain the Way through music?
Was Xi Kang's death inevitable?

zh: 大分流——18至19世纪欧亚经济发展差异
intro:
本次分享主要内容来自美国芝加哥大学历史系教授彭慕兰的学术著作《大分流：欧洲、中国及现代世界经济的发展》。与传统的欧洲中心论不同，彭慕兰主要以双向性对比讨论了在十八至十九世纪，是哪些因素的不同使得欧洲与亚洲的经济成长产生了巨大的差距。


引起兴趣的问题：

古代中国经济在什么时候最为强盛？

1750年中国经济与英国经济相比如何？

工业革命为什么发生在英国？

自然条件、制度、文化、巧合，哪个/哪些因素对于经济发展最为重要？


将会探讨的问题：

西欧经济从何时开始明显超越亚洲经济？

为何长江三角洲没有成为英格兰？为何英格兰没有成为长江三角洲？

如何看待几种不同的“欧洲中心论”（认为只有西欧经济才能产生工业转型的论点）？

西欧国家的海外殖民在经济发展中发挥了怎样的作用？

世界上人口稠密地区的贸易伙伴对经济发展有哪些影响？
en: The Great Divergence: Europe and Asia in the Eighteenth and Nineteenth Centuries
intro_en:
This session draws mainly on The Great Divergence: China, Europe, and the Making of the Modern World Economy, a scholarly work by Kenneth Pomeranz, professor of history at the University of Chicago. Departing from traditional Eurocentrism, Pomeranz uses two-way comparisons to discuss which differences in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries opened up the huge gap between economic growth in Europe and in Asia.

Questions to get us thinking:

When was the economy of ancient China at its strongest?

How did China's economy compare with Britain's in 1750?

Why did the Industrial Revolution happen in Britain?

Natural conditions, institutions, culture, chance: which of these matter most for economic development?

Questions we will explore:

When did the Western European economy begin clearly to outstrip the Asian economy?

Why did the Yangzi Delta not become England? Why did England not become the Yangzi Delta?

How should we view the various kinds of Eurocentrism (the argument that only Western European economies could have produced an industrial transformation)?

What role did Western European countries' overseas colonies play in their economic development?

How did trading partners affect economic development in the world's densely populated regions?

zh: 旧金山从何而来
intro:
本期内容比较轻松，希望介绍一点点旧金山背后的历史。具体来说主要想从地图入手，简单介绍旧金山这个城市和各个街区、景点背后的故事：旧金山是如何从最早的殖民者据点，一点点扩展成现在的样貌，中间有哪些大事件，这些事件对旧金山当下的城市分布有什么影响。


一些可以探讨的问题：
旧金山为什么叫『旧金山』？
为什么旧金山Market Street两侧街道完全对不齐？
金门公园是在模仿纽约中央公园么？
为什么旧金山这么多陡峭的斜坡道路？
旧金山为什么是世界上最著名的LGBTQ 人群聚居地？
大地震对现在的旧金山还有什么影响？
旧金山为什么没有高架和高速，几乎全是local？
en: Where San Francisco Came From
intro_en:
This session is on the lighter side: a little of the history behind San Francisco. Specifically, starting from maps, I'd like to give a brief introduction to the stories behind the city and its neighbourhoods and sights: how San Francisco grew bit by bit from an early colonial outpost into what it is today, what major events happened along the way, and how those events have shaped the layout of the city today.

Some questions we can explore:
Why is San Francisco called "Jiujinshan", the "Old Gold Mountain", in Chinese?
Why do the streets on either side of Market Street not line up at all?
Is Golden Gate Park an imitation of New York's Central Park?
Why does San Francisco have so many steep streets?
Why is San Francisco the world's most famous home for LGBTQ people?
What effects does the great earthquake still have on San Francisco today?
Why does San Francisco have no elevated roads or freeways, with almost everything local streets?

zh: 聊聊海外博物馆的中华文物
intro:
本次分享以Nelson Atkins Museum 为例，分享海外博物馆观展体验以及与中国文物的复杂关系。Nelson Atkins作为海外著名的中国文物展藏地，究竟有哪些藏品？受何人支持，又如何获取如此大量精致的藏品？海外博物馆的中华藏品的意义何在？

讨论内容如下：
Nelson Atkins 如何成立？
藏品有哪些？有什么与众不同的地方？
观展体验如何？
藏品从和收集而来？
海外藏展对于博物馆的意义

什么是好的博物馆/好的观展体验？
如何评价海外文物藏品的正当性？
未来博物馆会逐渐萧条吗？
en: Chinese Antiquities in Museums Abroad
intro_en:
Taking the Nelson-Atkins Museum as an example, this session shares the experience of visiting museums abroad and their complicated relationship with Chinese antiquities. The Nelson-Atkins is famous overseas for its Chinese collection: what exactly does it hold? Who backed it, and how did it acquire so many fine pieces? What is the significance of Chinese collections in museums abroad?

We will discuss:
How was the Nelson-Atkins founded?
What is in the collection, and what makes it distinctive?
What is it like to visit?
Where were the pieces collected from?
What overseas collections and exhibitions mean for museums

What makes a good museum, or a good museum visit?
How should we judge the legitimacy of antiquities held abroad?
Will museums gradually decline in the future?

zh: 武士的挽歌——会津战争
intro:
本次分享讲会津战争，作为明治维新开启序幕，戊辰战争的重要一环。为何新政府在江户开城之后仍然继续对东北用兵？

讨论内容如下：
"朝敌"以及政治合法性的转换有哪些原因？
会津战争的进程如何？失败有什么意义？
失败方会津藩的人有着何种不同的命运？
会津战争在日本造成了何种地域性差异？
日本人如何评价会津战争、戊辰战争，以及明治维新？
en: Elegy for the Samurai: The Aizu War
intro_en:
This session is about the Aizu War, an important part of the Boshin War, which opened the Meiji Restoration. Why did the new government keep sending troops into the north-east even after Edo Castle had surrendered?

We will discuss:
What lay behind the label "enemies of the court" and the shift in political legitimacy?
How did the Aizu War unfold? What did the defeat mean?
What different fates awaited the people of the defeated Aizu domain?
What regional differences did the Aizu War create in Japan?
How do the Japanese view the Aizu War, the Boshin War and the Meiji Restoration?

zh: 成也败也——郑国的建立和西东二周的兴替
intro:
在传统的观点中，美女褒姒的出现，导致了烽火戏诸侯的故事以及西周的灭亡。然而在现代人的视角里，红颜祸水的叙事已经失去了吸引力，也被越来越多的证据质疑。

在周朝较为重要的诸侯国中，郑国是立国最晚，也是唯一一个建立在两周之交的诸侯国。它在东周之初极为活跃，并直接参与了周郑交质，繻葛之战等一系列标志着天子权力衰落的事件之中。它为什么能在短短的时间内快速的崛起，又为什么衰落？

这一期我们将梳理西周灭亡和东周建立前后留下的记载以及文物，试图简单的重建这一段历史，并解释郑国的建立在这个过程中扮演的特殊角色。

我们将试着讨论以下的一些问题：
西周的灭亡经历了怎样的过程？西周和东周的历史是如何连接起来的？
郑国的是如何建立起来的？又是如何在西周灭亡之后站稳脚跟的？
郑国为何是首先和东周天子产生冲突的诸侯国？
为什么东周的天子几乎对国家没有实际的控制？
en: Rise and Fall: The Founding of Zheng and the Eastern and Western Zhou
intro_en:
In the traditional view, the appearance of the beautiful Bao Si led to the story of the beacon fires lit to fool the lords and to the fall of the Western Zhou. To modern eyes, however, the narrative of the femme fatale has lost its appeal, and more and more evidence calls it into question.

Among the more important vassal states of the Zhou, Zheng was the last to be founded, and the only one established at the transition from Western to Eastern Zhou. It was extremely active at the start of the Eastern Zhou and was directly involved in a series of events that marked the decline of the Son of Heaven's power, such as the exchange of hostages between Zhou and Zheng and the Battle of Xuge. Why was it able to rise so quickly, and why did it decline?

In this session we will go through the records and artefacts left from around the fall of the Western Zhou and the founding of the Eastern Zhou, try to reconstruct this period of history in simple terms, and explain the special role the founding of Zheng played in the process.

We will try to discuss the following questions:
How did the Western Zhou fall? How are the histories of the Western and Eastern Zhou connected?
How was Zheng founded, and how did it establish itself after the fall of the Western Zhou?
Why was Zheng the first vassal state to come into conflict with the Eastern Zhou king?
Why did the Eastern Zhou kings have almost no real control over the realm?

zh: 倭国变日本，倭王成天皇
intro:
“夜发熟田津，乘船待月明。潮来月忽出，趁早划船行。”

这首诗出自日本的《万叶集》，诗人此时跟随着一支庞大的远征军。这支军队由日本女王亲自率领，浩浩荡荡向西航行，准备和大唐决一死战。

等等，日本和唐朝进行过战争吗？为什么日本天皇是个女的？还有，日本为什么要进攻唐朝？他们后来赢了吗？

古坟时代和飞鸟时代的日本，常常不为人所知。但这段历史并不枯燥，既有剧情荒诞的故事，也有性格奇特的人物。在这次分享中，我们大致捋一捋四世纪至七世纪的日本，带大家走进那个风云变幻、万物革新的时代。

这次分享，我们会解答下面几个问题：

- 南北朝时期，日本向中国朝贡过吗？
- 日本的第一个天皇是谁？
- 日本有没有过女天皇？
- 有人杀死过天皇吗？
- 隋朝和日本有没有过交互？
- 日本和唐朝发生过战争吗？
- 波多野结衣为什么姓波多？

尤其是最后一个问题，非常重要，值得深入探讨。这次活动的互动猜谜环节被放到了前面，希望大家尽早入场哟！
en: From Wa to Japan, from King of Wa to Emperor
intro_en:
"Setting out by night from Nikitatsu, we board our ships and wait for the moon. The tide comes in, the moon suddenly rises: now, let us row out early."

This poem comes from Japan's Man'yōshū. At the time the poet was with a huge expeditionary force, led in person by the Japanese queen, sailing west in great array to fight Tang China to the death.

Wait, did Japan ever go to war with the Tang? Why was the Japanese emperor a woman? And why would Japan attack the Tang? Did they win?

Japan in the Kofun and Asuka periods is often little known. But this history is far from dull: it has stories with absurd plots and characters with strange personalities. In this session we will roughly trace Japan from the fourth to the seventh century, taking you into an age of turbulence and sweeping renewal.

In this session we will answer the following questions:

- Did Japan send tribute to China during the Northern and Southern Dynasties?
- Who was Japan's first emperor?
- Has Japan ever had a female emperor?
- Has anyone ever killed an emperor?
- Did the Sui dynasty have any dealings with Japan?
- Did Japan ever go to war with the Tang?
- Why is Hatano Yui's surname Hatano?

The last question in particular is very important and deserves in-depth discussion. The interactive quiz has been moved to the start of the session this time, so please join early!

zh: 闪电和先辈：君士坦丁堡的1453和2023
intro:
2023年5月28日，埃尔多安第三次当选土耳其总统。据新华社报道，他当晚发表讲话感谢选民支持，表示不会辜负支持者的信任。他同时承诺为土耳其下一个建国一百周年而努力工作。

2023年5月29日，伊斯坦布尔举行庆祝攻陷君士坦丁堡570周年活动。与此同时，雅典也有相应的小规模君士坦丁堡陷落570周年的纪念活动。
本次分享将以这两件事为背景，讨论1453年君士坦丁堡陷落与2023年土耳其大选的细节故事。

引起兴趣的问题：
15世纪除了君士坦丁堡陷落之外，还有哪些大事发生？
君士坦丁堡攻防的双方，奥斯曼苏丹穆罕默德二世和罗马帝国皇帝君士坦丁十一世分别扮演了什么角色？二人分别有什么能力和特质？
茨维格的《人类的群星闪耀时》如何描写君士坦丁堡的陷落？你知道哪些描写君士坦丁堡陷落的文学作品？
土耳其今天的政局是什么样的？分别有什么不同的党派？
埃尔多安为什么能合法连任第三届总统？


本次会讨论到的问题：
穆罕默德二世进攻君士坦丁堡做了哪些准备？
末代皇帝君士坦丁十一世能力如何？他做了哪些防御的努力？
君士坦丁堡攻城战有哪些细节故事？
土耳其现在的政治局势是什么样子的？
2017年的土耳其修宪对今天造成什么样的影响？
en: Lightning and Forebears: Constantinople in 1453 and 2023
intro_en:
On 28 May 2023, Erdoğan was elected president of Turkey for the third time. According to Xinhua, he gave a speech that evening thanking voters for their support and saying he would not let his supporters' trust down. He also pledged to work hard towards Turkey's next centenary.

On 29 May 2023, Istanbul held celebrations marking the 570th anniversary of the conquest of Constantinople. Meanwhile, Athens held smaller commemorations of the 570th anniversary of the fall of Constantinople.
Against the backdrop of these two events, this session will discuss the stories and details of the fall of Constantinople in 1453 and of Turkey's 2023 election.

Questions to get us thinking:
Apart from the fall of Constantinople, what other major events happened in the fifteenth century?
What roles did the two sides in the siege, the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II and the Roman emperor Constantine XI, play? What abilities and qualities did each have?
How does Stefan Zweig's Decisive Moments in History depict the fall of Constantinople? What other literary works about the fall of Constantinople do you know?
What is the political situation in Turkey today? What are the different parties?
How was Erdoğan able to be lawfully re-elected to a third term?

Questions this session will discuss:
What preparations did Mehmed II make for his attack on Constantinople?
How capable was the last emperor, Constantine XI? What efforts did he make at defence?
What stories and details are there from the siege of Constantinople?
What is the political situation in Turkey today?
What effect has the 2017 Turkish constitutional amendment had on the present day?

zh: 宫泽贤治《银河铁道之夜》
intro:
旧说天河与海通。近世有人居海渚者，每年八月有浮槎去来，不失期，人有奇志，立飞阁于槎上，多赍粮、乘槎而去。 ——晋·张华《博物志》卷十

本次分享将介绍日本童话作家宫泽贤治及其代表作品《银河铁道之夜》。特别活动：将在本次参与提问、讨论的朋友中随机抽取一位送出中文版《银河铁道之夜》。（分享者包邮费，限美国）

引起兴趣的问题：
“纵浮槎来，浮槎去，不相逢。” 中国古代都有哪些和天上沟通的故事？
其他国家有哪些和天上交流的神话故事？
你听说过宫泽贤治吗？如果是，是通过什么途径知道他的？
银河、群星为什么广泛在文学作品中出现？是为什么，有什么用意？
同理，车站、铁路为什么广泛在文学作品中出现？是为什么，有什么用意？
日本大正时代遭遇过什么危机？
本次将讨论到的问题：
宫泽贤治是一个什么样的人？
《银河铁道之夜》讲了一个什么样的故事？
宫泽贤治的创作风格和他的生平经历有什么关系？
宫泽贤治的诗歌作品有何独特的风格？

en: Miyazawa Kenji's Night on the Galactic Railroad
intro_en:
An old account says the Heavenly River connects with the sea. In recent times there was a man living on an island in the sea who saw a raft come and go every eighth month without fail. Being a man of unusual ambition, he built a flying pavilion on the raft, took plenty of provisions, and set off on it. -- Zhang Hua of the Jin, Record of Diverse Matters, juan 10

This session introduces the Japanese children's author Miyazawa Kenji and his best-known work, Night on the Galactic Railroad. Special event: one person will be drawn at random from those who ask questions or join the discussion to receive a Chinese edition of Night on the Galactic Railroad. (Postage paid by the speaker; US only.)

Questions to get us thinking:
"Though the raft may come and the raft may go, still we do not meet." What stories are there in ancient China of communicating with the heavens?
What myths do other countries have about communicating with the heavens?
Have you heard of Miyazawa Kenji? If so, how did you come to know of him?
Why do the Milky Way and the stars appear so widely in literature? What is the reason, and what do they signify?
Likewise, why do stations and railways appear so widely in literature? What is the reason, and what do they signify?
What crises did Japan face in the Taishō era?
Questions this session will discuss:
What kind of man was Miyazawa Kenji?
What story does Night on the Galactic Railroad tell?
How is Miyazawa Kenji's style related to his life?
What is distinctive about Miyazawa Kenji's poetry?

zh: 日本的世界观：200年来的变化
intro:
本次分享来自剑桥日本史主编马里乌斯詹森一本小书《日本的世界观：200年来的变化》。主要选取了德川幕府时期，明治维新时期和二战前后的三个时间切片，探讨日本人在这三个时代对于世界的认识，产生的变化以及对日本后续发展的意义。虽然听起来话题很大，但切入点很具体。詹森每个时代都选取了一个不那么知名的人物，从他们的个人经历入手，介绍了那个时代日本人是如何认知世界的。本次分享这次分享相对侧重17和18世纪的内容。


一些值得探讨的问题：
近代以前日本人如何看待中国的政权和欧洲的政权？
日本知识分子如何看待中国文化？他们如何认知自己在中国文化圈中的位置？
德川幕府时期为什么会有一小撮日本人通晓荷兰语并且翻译了大量西方科学著作？这些人的事业对后来日本经历的剧变有什么影响么？
鸦片战争之后，黑船来航之前日本是否意识到了世界的变化？他们有什么对策？
为什么明治维新之后核心领导层选择远离政治中心去周游列国一年多时间？他们都做了什么？见到了谁？这对后来明治维新的路线选择有影响吗？
日本明治维新之后崛起的日本如何重新认识自己在东亚的地位？
日本战后对世界的认知经历了什么样的变化？日本人如何看待美军基地/安保协定/宪法第九条对日本现在的影响？
en: Japan's View of the World: Two Hundred Years of Change
intro_en:
This session draws on a short book by Marius Jansen, general editor of The Cambridge History of Japan: Japan and Its World: Two Centuries of Change. It takes three slices of time, the Tokugawa shogunate, the Meiji Restoration, and the years around the Second World War, and explores how the Japanese of each era understood the world, how that understanding changed, and what it meant for Japan's later development. Although the topic sounds vast, the approach is very concrete: for each era Jansen picks a less famous figure and, starting from that person's own experiences, shows how the Japanese of the time perceived the world. This session will focus relatively more on the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

Some questions worth exploring:
Before the modern era, how did the Japanese view the Chinese and European powers?
How did Japanese intellectuals view Chinese culture? How did they see their own place within the Chinese cultural sphere?
Why, under the Tokugawa shogunate, did a small group of Japanese know Dutch and translate a large number of Western scientific works? Did their work have any influence on the upheavals Japan later went through?
After the Opium War but before the arrival of the Black Ships, was Japan aware that the world was changing? What did they do about it?
Why, after the Meiji Restoration, did the core leadership choose to leave the political centre and tour the world for more than a year? What did they do, and whom did they meet? Did this affect the course the Meiji Restoration later took?
How did Japan, rising after the Meiji Restoration, rethink its position in East Asia?
How did Japan's understanding of the world change after the war? How do the Japanese see the effects of the US bases, the security treaty and Article 9 of the constitution on Japan today?

zh: Medz Yeghern and Hayastan ——亚美尼亚大屠杀
intro:
4月24日是亚美尼亚大屠杀纪念日。本次分享将介绍这一事件的背景，亚美尼亚人的历史，以及奥斯曼、土耳其在其中扮演的角色。

引起兴趣的问题：
亚美尼亚是一个什么样的国家？
这一事件被称为”种族灭绝“是否合理？
“纳卡问题”为何成为一个延续到今日的冲突？
本次分享将讨论到的问题：
亚美尼亚人是如何形成的？
奥斯曼帝国的坦齐马特改革有什么成效？
现代土耳其国家和奥斯曼帝国有什么关系？
恩维尔帕夏和凯末尔帕夏分别做了什么？
青年土耳其党人和联合进步委员会在大屠杀中发挥了什么作用？
en: Medz Yeghern and Hayastan: The Armenian Genocide
intro_en:
24 April is Armenian Genocide Remembrance Day. This session will introduce the background to these events, the history of the Armenian people, and the roles played by the Ottoman Empire and Turkey.

Questions to get us thinking:
What kind of country is Armenia?
Is it reasonable to call these events a "genocide"?
Why has the Nagorno-Karabakh question become a conflict that continues to this day?
Questions this session will discuss:
How did the Armenian people take shape?
What did the Ottoman Empire's Tanzimat reforms achieve?
What is the relationship between the modern Turkish state and the Ottoman Empire?
What did Enver Pasha and Mustafa Kemal Pasha each do?
What role did the Young Turks and the Committee of Union and Progress play in the genocide?

zh: 清末银元概览
intro:
本期将介绍并讨论清末龙洋的缘起和历史，并介绍龙洋的不同品类和缘由。
问题：
1. 为什么要制造机制币，龙型图样的缘由
2. 为什么各省有不同种类的龙洋，他们的样式和珍稀程度又是怎样的
3. 圆两之争是怎么回事，“一圆”是怎么来的
4. 清朝最后发行了全国统一的龙洋吗
en: An Overview of Late-Qing Silver Dollars
intro_en:
This session will introduce and discuss the origins and history of the dragon dollars of the late Qing, and introduce their different varieties and how they came about.
Questions:
1. Why were machine-struck coins made, and why the dragon design?
2. Why did different provinces issue different kinds of dragon dollars, and what are their designs and rarity like?
3. What was the dispute between the yuan and the tael, and where did the "one yuan" come from?
4. Did the Qing eventually issue a nationally unified dragon dollar?

zh: 沧浪亭疑案
intro:
苏州最古老的园林沧浪亭是如何得名的？
始建于北宋中期的沧浪亭后来有着怎样的命运？它与庆历新政、变法兴衰、宋室南渡有着怎样的关联？
这座旷世园林见证了何种家族兴衰？它的几任主人又经历了怎样的身世浮沉？
时过境迁，曾经的故事已经湮没于岁月的长河，传世的文献中也遗失了详细的记载，历史却仍在空白处留下了蛛丝马迹……
en: The Mystery of the Canglang Pavilion
intro_en:
How did the Canglang Pavilion, Suzhou's oldest garden, get its name?
Built in the middle of the Northern Song, what became of the Canglang Pavilion later? How was it connected with the Qingli Reforms, the rise and fall of the reform movement, and the Song court's flight south?
What rises and falls of families did this matchless garden witness? And what reversals of fortune did its successive owners go through?
Times have changed, and the old stories have sunk into the long river of years; the surviving texts have lost the detailed records, yet history has still left faint traces in the gaps...

zh: 《贝奥武甫》
intro:
勇士们，让我们欢聚在烟霞部落的长屋里，举起牛角酒杯尽情畅饮吧！我要讲一讲高特国王贝奥武甫的故事，让诸位回到那个黑暗而奇幻的时代。1500年前，一个沼泽怪物狂暴地进入了宴会大厅，杀死了30名勇士。12年后，海平面上出现了高特人的船帆，这就是贝奥武甫传奇的开始。

啊！贝奥武甫！德意志的民族象征，丹麦人的伟大英雄。来自高特的武士国王啊，英格兰的吟游诗人仍然把你传唱！

贝奥武甫在历史上真的存在吗？他到底是德国人，瑞典人，丹麦人，还是英国人？贝奥武甫的财宝现在在哪里？守护财宝的火龙如今在何处？这部史诗是何时被发现的？它为什么影响了如今的英国政坛？

胜利不能靠求神拜佛，只有强壮的双臂才能赶走妖魔鬼怪。勇士们，让我们放下长剑，听一听贝奥武甫的传奇吧！

参考书籍：

《贝奥武甫》(冯象译)

《史诗大陆：欧洲历史的血与火》(尼古拉斯·朱伯)

《牛津英国史》(肯尼斯·O·摩根)

《History of Britain and Ireland: The Definitive Visual Guide》(DK)
en: Beowulf
intro_en:
Warriors, let us gather in the longhouse of the Yanxia tribe, raise our drinking horns and drink our fill! I shall tell the tale of Beowulf, king of the Geats, and take you back to that dark and fantastical age. Fifteen hundred years ago, a monster from the fens burst into the mead hall in a rage and killed thirty warriors. Twelve years later, the sails of the Geats appeared on the horizon, and so the legend of Beowulf began.

Ah, Beowulf! National symbol of the Germans, great hero of the Danes. Warrior king of the Geats, the bards of England still sing of you!

Did Beowulf really exist? Was he German, Swedish, Danish or English? Where is Beowulf's treasure now? Where is the fire dragon that guarded it today? When was the epic discovered? And why has it influenced British politics today?

Victory does not come from praying to the gods; only strong arms can drive away monsters and demons. Warriors, let us lay down our swords and hear the legend of Beowulf!

Reading:

Beowulf (translated by Feng Xiang)

Epic Continent: Adventures in the Great Stories of Europe (Nicholas Jubber)

The Oxford History of Britain (Kenneth O. Morgan)

History of Britain and Ireland: The Definitive Visual Guide (DK)

zh: 复仇的王子们和西域的钥匙
intro:
可以提前讨论的问题：
您印象里的西域历史上有过哪些管理机构/政权/著名的人和事？

在分享中我们将讨论：
十六国最后的终点是在何时何地？

从五十余国到安西四镇，汉唐期间的西域发生了什么？

戊己校尉从汉代设置以来，一直到十六国时期的割据政权都在继承，为什么统一北方的北魏却放弃了？

除了继承了中原的北魏，南北朝时期的西域还有哪些玩家？

为了经营西域，北魏做出了哪些尝试？
en: Avenging Princes and the Key to the Western Regions
intro_en:
Questions to discuss in advance:
What administrative bodies, regimes, and famous people and events in the history of the Western Regions come to mind?

In the session we will discuss:
When and where did the Sixteen Kingdoms finally come to an end?

From more than fifty states to the Four Garrisons of Anxi: what happened in the Western Regions between the Han and the Tang?

The office of the Wuji Colonel, first set up in the Han, was kept on by every regime down to the breakaway states of the Sixteen Kingdoms. Why did the Northern Wei, which unified the north, abandon it?

Apart from the Northern Wei, heir to the Central Plains, who were the other players in the Western Regions during the Northern and Southern Dynasties?

What did the Northern Wei try in order to manage the Western Regions?

zh: 梦中的彩云——《文心雕龙》
intro:
本次分享将介绍并讨论著名的文学批评著作《文心雕龙》以及其作者刘勰的生平故事。

问题：
刘勰是谁？他的生平如何？
《文心雕龙》讲了什么内容？
en: Coloured Clouds in a Dream: The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons
intro_en:
This session will introduce and discuss the famous work of literary criticism The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons, and the life of its author, Liu Xie.

Questions:
Who was Liu Xie? What was his life like?
What does The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons discuss?

zh: 日本纯爱文学
intro:
本次分享将讲述以市川拓司为代表的日本纯爱文学，介绍相关的作品。

问题：
纯爱小说有什么特点？
哪些群体的追捧早就了纯爱小说的市场？
你如何看待纯爱小说？
这类文学作品对现实有何参考意义？

《恋爱写真》
《在世界中心呼唤爱》
《情书》
en: Japanese Pure-Love Fiction
intro_en:
This session covers Japanese pure-love fiction, represented by Ichikawa Takuji, and introduces related works.

Questions:
What are the characteristics of pure-love novels?
Which readers' enthusiasm created the market for pure-love novels?
What do you think of pure-love novels?
What relevance do works of this kind have to real life?
Books:
Be With You
Heavenly Forest
Socrates in Love
Love Letter

zh: 爱的艺术
intro:
在前两次分享《家庭、私有制和国家的起源》和《伦理学》中，我们分别从宏观的角度讨论了家庭在不同时代的组织形式，从个人的角度讨论了人的感性和理性应该如何运用，以及定义善恶。

最近一部广泛传播的真人秀《再见爱人 第二季》已经完结，它引起了比较广泛的讨论，是一个值得讨论的话题。

本次分享将以弗洛姆《爱的艺术》一书内容为引导，探讨现代社会婚姻爱情中存在的问题和错位，结合之前分享中的讨论，进行更加深入的思考。

参考内容：
弗洛姆《爱的艺术》
罗兰·米勒《亲密关系》
再见爱人 第二季
再见爱人 第一季
en: The Art of Loving
intro_en:
In our previous two sessions, on The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State and on Spinoza's Ethics, we discussed, from a broad historical perspective, the forms the family has taken in different eras, and, from the individual's perspective, how human feeling and reason ought to be used and how good and evil are defined.

The widely watched reality show See You Again (Season 2) has just ended. It sparked a good deal of discussion and is a topic worth talking about.

This session takes Erich Fromm's The Art of Loving as its guide to explore the problems and mismatches in love and marriage in modern society, and builds on the discussions of earlier sessions to think about them more deeply.

References:
Erich Fromm, The Art of Loving
Rowland Miller, Intimate Relationships
See You Again, Season 2
See You Again, Season 1

zh: 我将一如既往——斯宾诺莎《伦理学》
intro:
本次分享将以斯宾诺莎《伦理学》为主，分享讨论斯宾诺莎的思想，对前后时代的影响。

问题：
伦理学是什么
《伦理学》这本书讲的是伦理学吗？
斯宾诺莎有什么其他主要思想？
斯宾诺莎的思想对后世有什么影响？

en: I Shall Carry On: Spinoza's Ethics
intro_en:
This session centres on Spinoza's Ethics, discussing Spinoza's thought and its influence on the eras before and after him.

Questions:
What is ethics?
Is the book Ethics actually about ethics?
What were Spinoza's other main ideas?
What influence did Spinoza's thought have on later generations?

zh: 社会化抚养？——《家庭、私有制和国家的起源》
intro:
本次分享将以恩格斯阅读摩尔根的《古代社会》而作的《家庭、私有制和国家的起源》为分享内容，讨论最近引起争议的社会化抚养话题。
讨论问题：
家庭单位是怎样随着时代变革而产生的？
氏族单位在家庭产生和演变过程中起到什么作用？
不同地区的家庭单位经历过什么样的变化过程？
社会制度和家庭制度之间有着何种关系？现代社会对家庭制度造成什么改变？

en: Socialised Child-Rearing? The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State
intro_en:
This session looks at The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State, which Engels wrote after reading Lewis Henry Morgan's Ancient Society, and uses it to discuss the recently controversial idea of socialised child-rearing.
Questions for discussion:
How did the family unit arise as the eras changed?
What role did the clan play in the emergence and evolution of the family?
What changes did the family unit go through in different regions?
What is the relationship between the social system and the family system? How has modern society changed the family system?
Is socialised child-rearing feasible? If so, is it the only answer?

Reading list:
The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State
Ancient Society, or Researches in the Lines of Human Progress from Savagery through Barbarism to Civilization
Patriarchy and Capitalism

zh: 日本从哪里来？——弥生时代和日本王权的诞生
intro:
本期我们将会走进神秘的日本弥生时代，探索日本的起源。


我们中国有一些传说：方士徐福东渡大海，为秦始皇求取仙丹。但他没有取回仙丹，而是在海外建立了日本国。那么，日本人从哪里来？日本人的祖先真的是徐福吗？日本何时成为了一个国家？它最初的名字是什么？


玩过《古墓丽影》的玩家或许记得：日本有一个神秘的邪马台国，女王卑弥呼能够控制风暴，用神力统治日本岛。那么，邪马台是一个真实的国家吗？卑弥呼真的可以呼风唤雨吗？


我们知道，唐宋以来日本和中国交流频繁。但日本是什么时候开始和中国接触的呢？它是中国的朝贡国吗？


我们这次沙龙会一一为大家解答这些问题，最后还会有一些有趣的互动活动。欢迎大家参与！


参考书目：

《王权的诞生》

《史记》

《汉书》

《三国志》
en: Where Did Japan Come From? The Yayoi Period and the Birth of Royal Power
intro_en:
In this session we step into Japan's mysterious Yayoi period to explore the origins of Japan.


There is a Chinese legend that the alchemist Xu Fu crossed the sea to the east in search of an elixir of immortality for the First Emperor of Qin. He never brought the elixir back; instead, he founded the state of Japan overseas. So where did the Japanese come from? Was Xu Fu really their ancestor? When did Japan become a state? What was its original name?


Anyone who has played Tomb Raider may remember that Japan had a mysterious kingdom called Yamatai, whose queen Himiko could command storms and ruled the Japanese islands with divine power. So was Yamatai a real kingdom? Could Himiko really summon wind and rain?


We know that Japan and China were in frequent contact from the Tang and Song dynasties onward. But when did Japan first come into contact with China? Was it a tributary state of China?


In this salon we will answer these questions one by one, and finish with some fun interactive activities. Everyone is welcome to join!


Reading list:

The Birth of Royal Power

Records of the Grand Historian

Book of Han

Records of the Three Kingdoms

zh: 日出江花——长者在罗马尼亚
intro:
前中国国家主席江泽民于2022年11月30日去世。本次分享将以江泽民于1971-1972年接受罗马尼亚援助任务，奔赴罗马尼亚的故事为背景，从历史进程和自我奋斗两方面，揭示整个事件的发展和相关人员的决策路线。

相关问题：
为什么1970年代中国要援助罗马尼亚？
罗马尼亚是一个什么样的国家？
“援助”罗马尼亚的难点在哪里？
对罗马尼亚的援助取得了什么成果？
你对江泽民有多大的了解？
如何看待网络上对江泽民的二次创作？

《江泽民文选》
en: The Sun Rises on the River Flowers: The Elder in Romania
intro_en:
Former Chinese President Jiang Zemin died on 30 November 2022. This session is set against the story of Jiang Zemin's assignment in 1971–1972 to help with China's aid to Romania, which took him to Romania, and looks at both the course of history and personal striving to show how the whole affair unfolded and the decisions made by those involved.

Related questions:
Why did China provide aid to Romania in the 1970s?
What kind of country was Romania?
What made "aiding" Romania difficult?
What did the aid to Romania achieve?
How much do you know about Jiang Zemin?
What do you make of the online fan creations about Jiang Zemin?
Reading list:

zh: 这就是奥斯维辛——听普里莫·莱维说
intro:
普里莫·莱维是意大利作家，曾有过奥斯维辛集中营的悲惨经历。本次分享将以他的几本回忆录为框架，分享奥斯维辛集中营中的一个普通人视角。

问题如下：
- 当事人是如何面对集中营生活的？
- “为什么不抵抗？为什么不跑？” 有过集中营生活的人如何面对别人的指责？
- 集中营的真实生活是什么样的？有什么样的形态？
- 其他社会中有哪些其他集中营式的生活？

参考书目：
- I sommersi e i salvati  被淹没与被拯救的 The Drowned and the Saved
- Se non ora, quando? 若非此时，何时？ If Not Now, When?
- Se questo è un uomo 如果这是一个人 / Survival in Auschwitz 奥斯维辛的幸存者
- La tregua休战 / The Reawakening 再度觉醒
en: This Is Auschwitz: Listening to Primo Levi
intro_en:
Primo Levi was an Italian writer who lived through the horrors of the Auschwitz concentration camp. Using several of his memoirs as a framework, this session presents Auschwitz from the point of view of an ordinary person.

Questions:
- How did those who were there cope with life in the camp?
- "Why didn't you resist? Why didn't you run?" How did camp survivors respond to such accusations from others?
- What was real life in the camp like? What forms did it take?
- What other camp-like forms of life have existed in other societies?

Reading list:
- I sommersi e i salvati / The Drowned and the Saved
- Se non ora, quando? / If Not Now, When?
- Se questo è un uomo / If This Is a Man (Survival in Auschwitz)
- La tregua / The Truce (The Reawakening)

zh: 2022年度总结
intro:
2022年风云变幻，我们见证了很多重大的事件。从今年二月份起，我们这个主题分享活动累计举办了三十五次。涉及的主题大多数为历史、文学以及相关话题。

值得高兴的是它持续地办了下去。不足之处在于后期形成了一定的路径依赖，因为分享者参与者的工作学习安排，很难投入更多的时间。

因此，我们计划在今年的最后一个周五，总结一下之前每期分享的成功和不足之处。希望可以客观地分析，哪里需要进行改动，既让分享者讲出自己的乐趣，也让所有参与者更能感受到乐趣，每个人都有新的收获。
en: Review of the Year 2022
intro_en:
2022 was a turbulent year, and we witnessed many major events. Since February this year, this talk series has held thirty-five sessions in all, mostly on history, literature and related topics.

We are glad that it has kept going. The downside is that in the later sessions it settled into a certain path dependence, because the work and study commitments of speakers and participants made it hard for them to put in more time.

So on the last Friday of the year we plan to review what went well and what fell short in each of our past sessions. We hope to analyse objectively what needs to change, so that speakers can talk about what they enjoy, all participants can enjoy it more, and everyone comes away with something new.

zh: “上帝决不饶恕”——韩剧《第5共和国》
intro:
本次分享将介绍韩剧《第5共和国》。讨论自1979年10月26日朴正熙被暗杀到1988年2月25日卢泰愚就任总统为止的第五共和国时期的历史。
联系前两次的分享，《路易波拿巴的五月十八日》和《日本陆军的轨迹》，从不同的角度，可以看到这些事件的一些相似性。鉴于本剧在网络上的影响力和传播方式，其中一些梗的爆火也值得讨论。
“上帝决不饶恕”（Deus Non Vult）是本剧的主题曲，也反映了剧作者对于这一历史时期的态度。
主要的分享内容：
朴正熙是如何被刺杀的。他对韩国造成了什么影响。
金载圭为什么要刺杀朴正熙。
全斗焕是如何在朴正熙死后的混乱局面中夺取权力的。
en: 'God Will Never Forgive': The Korean Drama The Fifth Republic
intro_en:
This session introduces the Korean drama The Fifth Republic and discusses the history of the Fifth Republic period, from the assassination of Park Chung-hee on 26 October 1979 to Roh Tae-woo's inauguration as president on 25 February 1988.
Linking it to our two previous sessions, on The Eighteenth Brumaire of Louis Bonaparte and The Path of the Imperial Japanese Army, we can see some similarities between these events from different angles. Given the show's influence online and the way it has spread, the viral popularity of some of its memes is also worth discussing.
"God Will Never Forgive" (Deus Non Vult) is the show's theme song, and it also reflects the writers' attitude towards this period of history.
Main content of the session:
How Park Chung-hee was assassinated, and what impact he had on South Korea.
Why Kim Jae-gyu assassinated Park Chung-hee.
How Chun Doo-hwan seized power in the chaos that followed Park Chung-hee's death.

zh: 日本陆军的轨迹
intro:
本次分享将介绍川田稔的《日本陆军的轨迹》，讲述1931到1942年间日本陆军的变革以及对政治的影响。
在本书中，将满洲事变以后作为一个政治组织化了的陆军称之为昭和陆军。虽然以往也有山县有朋以及桂太郎，寺内正毅，田中义一等陆军领导人作为个人试图掌握政治权力的先例。但是陆军作为一个组织试图控制政权，乃是一个新的动向。
en: The Path of the Imperial Japanese Army
intro_en:
This session introduces Kawada Minoru's The Path of the Imperial Japanese Army, which tells how the Japanese Army changed between 1931 and 1942 and how it affected politics.
The book calls the army after the Manchurian Incident, having become a political organisation, the "Shōwa Army". There had been earlier precedents of army leaders such as Yamagata Aritomo, Katsura Tarō, Terauchi Masatake and Tanaka Giichi trying as individuals to take political power. But the army trying, as an organisation, to control the government was a new development.

zh: 卡尔·马克思《路易·波拿巴的雾月十八日》
intro:
"黑格尔在某个地方说过，一切伟大的世界历史事变和人物，可以说都出现两次。他忘记补充一点：第一次是作为悲剧出现，第二次是作为笑剧出现。"

1848年革命是维多利亚时代的一个重要节点，对欧洲乃至世界的历史产生了重大的影响。本文文辞优美，思想深刻。本次分享将从中选择第一章和最后一章进行共读。

可以讨论的问题：

如何认识作品的文学艺术价值？
如何看待作者对于社会结构的分析？
1848年革命在法国有何波折？
作者如何看待1848年革命以及后续事件？
作者与雨果、波德莱尔等人对革命的理解有何不同？
en: Karl Marx, The Eighteenth Brumaire of Louis Bonaparte
intro_en:
"Hegel remarks somewhere that all great world-historical events and personages appear, so to speak, twice. He forgot to add: the first time as tragedy, the second time as farce."

The Revolution of 1848 was a major turning point of the Victorian era, with a profound impact on the history of Europe and indeed the world. This text is beautifully written and deeply thoughtful. In this session we will read its first and last chapters together.

Possible questions for discussion:

How should we assess the work's literary and artistic value?
What do you make of the author's analysis of social structure?
What twists and turns did the 1848 Revolution take in France?
How did the author view the 1848 Revolution and the events that followed?
How does the author's understanding of revolution differ from that of Hugo, Baudelaire and others?

intro_en:

zh: 宋神宗之死
intro:
元丰八年三月甲午，37岁的宋神宗去世。他因为任用王安石实行熙丰变法而闻名，又在死后被推翻之前推行的所有政策。  宋神宗去世后，北宋后期以及南宋政局多次发生反复，导致《神宗实录》多次重修，因此对神宗去世、哲宗即位这一历史事件的描述有很多不同来源，不同立场的不同版本。

我们将通过简要的背景人物介绍，以及共同阅读相关叙述，来了解不同立场的人对这一事件的描述，推断叙述的可信度，并试图还原事情的真相。

相关争议要点：
* 宰相王珪是否支持哲宗即位
* 次相蔡确是否有拥立哲宗的定策之功
* 宣仁皇后是否有意让次子雍王即位
* 次相蔡确是否有意支持雍王即位
en: The Death of Emperor Shenzong of Song
intro_en:
On the jiawu day of the third month of the eighth year of Yuanfeng (1085), Emperor Shenzong of Song died at the age of 37. He is known for employing Wang Anshi to carry out the Xifeng reforms, and after his death all the policies he had put in place were overturned. After Shenzong's death, the political situation of the late Northern Song and the Southern Song swung back and forth many times, and the Veritable Records of Shenzong were revised again and again. As a result, there are many different versions, from different sources and different standpoints, of the events surrounding Shenzong's death and Zhezong's accession.

Through brief introductions to the background and the people involved, and by reading the relevant accounts together, we will look at how people of different standpoints described these events, judge how credible each account is, and try to reconstruct what really happened.

Key points of controversy:
* Did the chief councillor Wang Gui support Zhezong's accession?
* Did the second councillor Cai Que deserve credit for securing Zhezong's enthronement?
* Did Empress Xuanren intend for her second son, the Prince of Yong, to take the throne?
* Did the second councillor Cai Que intend to support the Prince of Yong's accession?

zh: 将军与大树
intro:
本次分享将尝试一种新的方式，从游记和感想出发引出之后希望分享和讨论的话题。

一句话的陈述：分享者去了Sequoia & Kings Canyon National Park, 见到红杉木聚落的生态系统，想起庾信的《枯树赋》，模仿它也写了一篇“赋”。

将会讨论到以及希望讨论到的内容：
美国国家公园有什么游玩的必要吗？美国的国家公园是如何创立的？
作为美国创立的第三个国家公园，红杉国家公园有何特殊之处？
红杉的生态系统是如何形成的？有什么特殊之处？
庾信的《枯树赋》与红杉国家公园的树有什么联系？
现在是否还有写“赋”的必要，有什么意义？
en: The General and the Great Tree
intro_en:
This session tries a new format, starting from a travel account and personal reflections to lead into the topics we hope to share and discuss.

In one sentence: the speaker visited Sequoia & Kings Canyon National Park, saw the ecosystem of the giant sequoia groves, was reminded of Yu Xin's Rhapsody on a Withered Tree, and wrote a "rhapsody" (fu) of their own in imitation of it.

What we will discuss, and hope to discuss:
Are America's national parks worth visiting? How were America's national parks founded?
As the third national park established in the United States, what is special about Sequoia National Park?
How did the sequoia ecosystem form? What is special about it?
What is the connection between Yu Xin's Rhapsody on a Withered Tree and the trees of Sequoia National Park?
Is there still any need to write fu today, and what would be the point?

zh: 第一缕南风：晏殊和他的时代
intro:
本次分享将介绍北宋词人、政治家晏殊，以及庆历新政的相关历史。

一些将要讨论和引起思考的问题：
晏殊的词作品风格是怎样的？你能说出一两句他的作品么？
他在宋词的发展过程中扮演了什么样的角色？
晏殊和同时代的其他几位文豪词宗（欧阳修，范仲淹，柳永，张先等等）都是什么关系？晏殊的家庭生活是怎样的？
自小有神童之名的晏殊，人生真的是“富贵太平一生”么？
庆历新政的前因后果是什么？
时任同平章事的晏殊是怎么看待国家政务的？他是否参与了庆历新政？
晏殊在庆历三年到四年的时间里可能扮演了什么样的角色？
en: The First Southern Breeze: Yan Shu and His Times
intro_en:
This session introduces Yan Shu, the Northern Song ci poet and statesman, and the history of the Qingli Reforms.

Some questions we will discuss and that we hope will get you thinking:
What is the style of Yan Shu's ci poems? Can you quote a line or two of his work?
What role did he play in the development of Song ci?
What were Yan Shu's relationships with the other great writers and ci masters of his time (Ouyang Xiu, Fan Zhongyan, Liu Yong, Zhang Xian and others)? What was Yan Shu's family life like?
Known as a child prodigy from an early age, did Yan Shu really live "a lifetime of wealth, rank and peace"?
What were the causes and consequences of the Qingli Reforms?
How did Yan Shu, then serving as chief minister, view affairs of state? Did he take part in the Qingli Reforms?
What role might Yan Shu have played between the third and fourth years of Qingli?

zh: 张爱玲《留情》
intro:
本次将分享张爱玲短篇小说《留情》。有兴趣参与的朋友可以提前阅读。根据之前活动的经验，在共同的阅读中，可能会形成一种自己没有留意，但是讨论出来成为共识的东西。跟个人阅读的视角会略有不同。

由于小说偏长，本次将更多的时间放在文本阅读和讨论上。缩短自我介绍的时间，去掉作者介绍的时间。安排如下：
自我介绍环节（5-10mins）
参与者共读（40-70mins）
讨论（30-40mins）
en: Eileen Chang's Lingering Love
intro_en:
This session looks at Eileen Chang's short story Lingering Love. Anyone interested in joining is welcome to read it beforehand. From the experience of earlier sessions, reading together can produce something you might not have noticed on your own but that emerges as a shared understanding through discussion. It differs somewhat from what you see reading alone.

Because the story is fairly long, we will spend more time on reading and discussing the text this time, shortening the introductions and dropping the introduction to the author. The schedule is as follows:
Introductions (5–10 mins)
Group reading (40–70 mins)
Discussion (30–40 mins)

zh: 肝胆皆冰雪——张孝祥与南宋
intro:
本次分享将以南宋著名词人张孝祥的生平为主线，阅览张孝祥的平生经历和南宋初年的历史故事。

问题：
你最喜欢的宋词是哪一首？为什么让你动容？
宋高宗赵构和秦桧的关系是什么样的？他们是如何做出与金国议和的决策的？
金海陵王完颜亮希望统一天下，消灭南宋为何失败？
为什么南宋能取得采石大捷？
张孝祥有哪些代表作品？为什么张孝祥对苏轼如此推崇？
en: A Heart of Ice and Snow: Zhang Xiaoxiang and the Southern Song
intro_en:
Following the life of the famous Southern Song ci poet Zhang Xiaoxiang, this session surveys his experiences and the history of the early Southern Song.

Questions:
Which Song ci poem is your favourite? Why does it move you?
What was the relationship between Emperor Gaozong (Zhao Gou) and Qin Hui? How did they decide to make peace with the Jin?
Wanyan Liang, the Prince of Hailing of the Jin, hoped to unify the realm. Why did he fail to destroy the Southern Song?
Why was the Southern Song able to win the great victory at Caishi?
What are Zhang Xiaoxiang's major works? Why did Zhang Xiaoxiang admire Su Shi so much?

zh: 二十一世纪的历史同人作品
intro:
本次分享将叙述同人作品的起源发展和分类，讨论历史同人作品的发展原因和现状。

问题：
什么是同人作品（Fanfic）？如何看待读者的集体创作？
什么是历史同人？历史和同人作品是如何结合起来的？什么是OOC同人？
现今的同人作品是如何发展的？
同人作品的发展背后动机是什么？
同人作品拥有哪些分类？我们平常耳熟能详的作品中有哪些可以看作同人作品？
如何看待耽美同人（Slash Fanfic）的发展和”组CP“？
为什么耽美同人的创作者和受众主要都是女性？
en: Historical Fan Fiction in the Twenty-First Century
intro_en:
This session describes the origins, development and categories of fan fiction, and discusses why historical fan fiction has developed and where it stands today.

Questions:
What is fan fiction (fanfic)? What do you make of collective creation by readers?
What is historical fan fiction? How have history and fan fiction come together? What is OOC fan fiction?
How has fan fiction developed today?
What motivates the development of fan fiction?
What categories of fan fiction are there? Which familiar works could be seen as fan fiction?
What do you make of the growth of slash fanfic and "shipping"?
Why are both the creators and the audience of slash fiction mainly women?

zh: 桓君山之志事
intro:
本次分享将着重于东汉时期的两位学者桓谭和王充，介绍他们的著作《新论》和《论衡》中的精彩想法。如果时间充足，可以再对张衡和扬雄进行简单介绍。

问题：
《新论》反映了桓谭哪些方面的思想？
什么是形神说？
王充又是在什么背景下写下《论衡》？
两人成书和当时的时代背景有何联系？
如何看待古代的谶纬神学和科学认知？
在今天现代的角度如何重新审视东汉经学的争论？
en: The Aspirations of Huan Tan
intro_en:
This session focuses on two scholars of the Eastern Han, Huan Tan and Wang Chong, and introduces the brilliant ideas in their works, the New Treatise (Xinlun) and the Balanced Discourses (Lunheng). If time allows, we may also briefly introduce Zhang Heng and Yang Xiong.

Questions:
What aspects of Huan Tan's thought does the New Treatise reflect?
What is the theory of body and spirit?
In what context did Wang Chong write the Balanced Discourses?
How were the two men's works connected with the times they were written in?
What do you make of ancient prognostication theology and scientific understanding?
How might we re-examine the debates of Eastern Han classical scholarship from a modern perspective today?

zh: 金锁记
intro:
因为这周参与了非鱼剧社的话剧《金锁记》，准备分享活动的时间不是特别充足，所以索性这一期直接来分享张爱玲的这部《金锁记》，或引申到张爱玲的其他作品。

问题：
你对张爱玲的印象是什么？读过她的哪些作品？
张爱玲的身世对她的作品风格有什么影响？
张爱玲的作品有什么特点？
如何看待张爱玲的《金锁记》？以及王安忆将它改编成的话剧？
王安忆是谁啊？她有什么作品？
en: Eileen Chang's The Golden Cangue
intro_en:
Because I took part in the Feiyu Theatre Club's stage production of The Golden Cangue this week, I haven't had much time to prepare a session, so this time I will simply talk about Eileen Chang's The Golden Cangue, and perhaps extend the discussion to her other works.

Questions:
What is your impression of Eileen Chang? Which of her works have you read?
How did Eileen Chang's life story influence the style of her work?
What are the characteristics of Eileen Chang's writing?
What do you make of Eileen Chang's The Golden Cangue, and of Wang Anyi's stage adaptation of it?
Who is Wang Anyi, anyway? What has she written?

zh: J. D. Salinger - The Heart of a Broken Story
intro:
本次将分享美国作家杰罗姆·大卫·塞林格的短篇小说《破碎故事之心》。

参照第十五期分享，时间安排如下：
自我介绍环节（10-20mins）
主持人简单介绍作家（10-20mins）
参与者共读（30-40mins）
讨论（30-40mins）
共读和讨论可以伴随进行，读完一部分，就这一部分进行讨论。

在线阅读：
https://www.ae-lib.org.ua/texts/salinger__early_stories__en.htm#04

塞林格的其他有趣作品：
《麦田里的守望者》
《九故事》
en: J. D. Salinger: The Heart of a Broken Story
intro_en:
This session looks at The Heart of a Broken Story, a short story by the American writer J. D. Salinger.

Following session 15, the schedule is as follows:
Introductions (10–20 mins)
Brief introduction to the author by the host (10–20 mins)
Group reading (30–40 mins)
Discussion (30–40 mins)
Reading and discussion can go hand in hand: after reading a section, we discuss that section.

Read online:
https://www.ae-lib.org.ua/texts/salinger__early_stories__en.htm#04

Other interesting works by Salinger:
The Catcher in the Rye
Nine Stories

zh: 叫魂：1768年中国妖术大恐慌
intro:
剪掉头发，取人魂魄。一股妖风在大清盛世蔓延，一个疑案让百姓陷入了大恐慌。皇帝亲自指挥，官员纷纷出动。这个疑案到底是怎么回事？它的主谋究竟是谁？“剪辫案”发生的时期和今天的中国有什么相似之处？又有什么不同？

本次烟霞沙龙，主讲人屈直会给大家分享读书心得《叫魂：1768年中国妖术大恐慌》，带领大家探索一个危机重重的康乾盛世。分享之前，有几个问题值得大家思考：
- 你相信灵魂的存在吗？
- 你接触过哪些描绘妖术的艺术作品？
  - 小说？
  - 影视剧？
  - 游戏？
- 你听说过哪些关于魂魄的说法？
- 你对清朝和乾隆皇帝有哪些印象？
en: Soulstealers: The Chinese Sorcery Scare of 1768
intro_en:
Cut off a queue and steal a soul. An evil wind swept through the prosperous Qing, and a mysterious case threw the common people into a great panic. The emperor took personal command, and officials were sent out in force. What was really behind this case? Who was its mastermind? What does the period of the "queue-clipping cases" have in common with China today? And how is it different?

In this Yanxia salon, our speaker Qu Zhi will share his reading notes on Soulstealers: The Chinese Sorcery Scare of 1768, and lead us in exploring a High Qing era of Kangxi and Qianlong beset with crises. Before the session, here are a few questions worth thinking about:
- Do you believe souls exist?
- What works of art depicting sorcery have you come across?
  - Novels?
  - Films or TV series?
  - Games?
- What beliefs about the soul have you heard of?
- What are your impressions of the Qing dynasty and the Qianlong Emperor?

zh: 中文屋
intro:
Can a machine think? Engineers, scientists, and philosophers have been pondering this question ever since the earliest days of computers. 

The Chinese Room is one of the most famous (notorious) thought experiments in this field, perhaps second only to Alan Turing’s Imitation Game. Proposed in Berkeley in 1980, the Chinese Room is directed against computationalist theory of mind, and a version of strong AI theory that claims that machines can indeed think. 

Some of the questions we will dive into: 
What happens in the Chinese Room? 
Four decades later, can we apply the same critique to today’s AI? 
How does the charge of computationalism hold up against today’s neural network based AI?

zh: 近體詩格律淺析
intro:
本次分享将通过例证和互动的方式为大家浅解近体诗格律。


拋磚引玉：

古詩、古體詩、近體詩、新詩、律詩、絕句等等，它們之間的關系是怎樣的？我們讀的到底是什麽詩？

我們所說的格律，到底指什麽？『靜夜思』合律嗎？『鳥鳴澗』合律嗎？『登鸛雀樓』合律嗎？

為什麼很多古詩讀起來覺得拗口？

今人如何學習平仄和四聲？


今試以輕車快馬，一闢格律蹊徑。


主題：近體詩格律淺析

分享人：錢力，谷歌九歌詩社


自由討論數題：

近体诗和古体诗孰高孰下？

律诗为什么于唐代成形？

新诗值得提倡吗？

當代诗歌创作应用古韵还是新韵？

初学者如何进行近体诗创作？
en: A Primer on Regulated Verse
intro_en:
This session offers a brief introduction to the metrical rules of regulated verse, through examples and interaction.


Some questions to get us started:

Ancient poetry, old-style verse, regulated verse, modern poetry, lüshi, jueju and so on: how are they related to one another? What kind of poetry are we actually reading?

What exactly do we mean by metrical rules? Does "Quiet Night Thoughts" follow the rules? Does "Birds Calling in the Ravine"? Does "On Climbing Stork Tower"?

Why do so many classical poems feel awkward to read aloud?

How can people today learn level and oblique tones and the four tones?


Here we try, travelling light and fast, to open a path into the rules of versification.


Topic: A Primer on Regulated Verse

Speaker: Qian Li, Google Jiuge Poetry Society


A few questions for open discussion:

Which is superior, regulated verse or old-style verse?

Why did regulated verse take shape in the Tang dynasty?

Is modern poetry worth promoting?

Should poetry written today use the old rhymes or the new rhymes?

How should beginners go about writing regulated verse?

zh: 芥川龙之介《鼻子》
intro:
本次分享将简单介绍日本作家芥川龙之介，参与者共读他的短篇小说《鼻子》并进行讨论。时间安排如下：
自我介绍环节（10-20mins）
主持人简单介绍芥川龙之介（10-20mins）
参与者共读《鼻子》（30-40mins）
讨论（30-40mins）
共读和讨论可以伴随进行，读完一部分，就这一部分进行讨论。

感兴趣的朋友可以提前阅读。
鲁迅译《鼻子》： https://zh.m.wikisource.org/zh-hans/%E9%BC%BB%E5%AD%90

《罗生门》
《竹林中》
《山药粥》
《地狱变》
《杜子春》
en: Akutagawa Ryūnosuke's The Nose
intro_en:
This session gives a brief introduction to the Japanese writer Akutagawa Ryūnosuke, after which participants will read his short story The Nose together and discuss it. The schedule is as follows:
Introductions (10–20 mins)
Brief introduction to Akutagawa Ryūnosuke by the host (10–20 mins)
Group reading of The Nose (30–40 mins)
Discussion (30–40 mins)
Reading and discussion can go hand in hand: after reading a section, we discuss that section.

Anyone interested is welcome to read it beforehand.
Lu Xun's translation of The Nose: https://zh.m.wikisource.org/zh-hans/%E9%BC%BB%E5%AD%90

Other interesting works by Akutagawa Ryūnosuke:
Rashōmon
In a Grove
Yam Gruel
Hell Screen
Tu Tze-chun

zh: 鲲鹏安知鹪鹩
intro:
本次分享讲围绕晋司空张华进行分享、分析和讨论。


来自《博物志》小故事，猜猜这几个描述的是什么科学/常识内容？

• 今人梳头脱著衣时，有随梳解结有光者，亦有咤声。
• 地常动不止，譬如人在舟而坐，舟行而人不觉。天地四方皆海水相通，地在其中盖无几也。
• 昔日南貢四象，各有雌雄。其一雄死於九真，乃至南海百有餘日，其雌塗土著身，不飲食，穴草，長史問其所以，聞之輒流涕。
• 旧洛阳字作水边各，汉火行也，忌水，故去水而加佳。又魏于行次为土，水得土而流，土得水而柔，故复去佳加水，変雒为洛焉。
 

一些分享中可以带着思考的问题：

• 《博物志》的作者张华，为什么能从一个牧羊娃，在“上品无寒门，下品无势族”的西晋，做到了国家的实际决策者？
• 他是怎么跨越日趋森严的士庶区隔，得到自上而下的认可和接受的？
• 寒门出身，是否影响了张华的交游和决策？
• 除了《博物志》之外，张华还有留下了什么其他的作品？
• 是什么让晋武帝铁了心立“何不食肉糜”的傻儿子做国家的继承人？
 

分享之后可以讨论的问题：

• 西晋为什么无法维持长期的稳定统治？
• 张华是否有一个一贯的政治立场，如果有的话，是什么？
• 张华是否有可能化解晋惠帝的老婆和儿子（贾南风与愍怀太子）之间的矛盾？
• 西晋时期南北士人的分歧为什么难以达成和解？
• 玄学清谈和空谈误国之间有必然的关系么？
 

相关资料：
唐·房玄龄《晋书》
权家玉《魏晋政治与皇权传递》
罗宗强《玄学与魏晋士人心态》
仇鹿鸣《魏晋之际的政治权力与家族网络》
en: What Does the Great Roc Know of the Wren?
intro_en:
This session centres on Zhang Hua, Minister of Works of the Jin, with a talk, analysis and discussion.


Here are some short passages from the Treatise on Curiosities (Bowuzhi). Can you guess what scientific facts or common knowledge they describe?

• When people today comb their hair or take off their clothes, sometimes there are sparks as the comb undoes the knots, and sometimes a crackling sound.
• The earth moves constantly and never stops, just as a person sitting in a boat does not feel the boat moving. On all four sides of heaven and earth the seas are connected, and the land in their midst is only small.
• Long ago Rinan sent four elephants as tribute, each with its mate. One of the males died in Jiuzhen. More than a hundred days later, when they reached Nanhai, its mate smeared mud over its body, would neither eat nor drink, and burrowed into the grass. When the chief clerk asked about it, the elephant wept as soon as it heard.
• The "Luo" of Luoyang was once written with the water radical beside 各. The Han ruled by the element of Fire and shunned water, so the water radical was removed and 隹 added. Then the Wei ruled by the element of Earth; water flows when it meets earth, and earth softens when it meets water, so 隹 was removed again and the water radical added, changing 雒 back into 洛.


Some questions to keep in mind during the talk:

• How did Zhang Hua, author of the Treatise on Curiosities, rise from shepherd boy to the de facto decision-maker of the state in the Western Jin, an age when "the top ranks held no one of humble birth, and the bottom ranks no one from a powerful clan"?
• How did he cross the ever more rigid divide between the gentry and commoners and win acceptance and recognition from above and below?
• Did his humble origins affect Zhang Hua's social circle and his decisions?
• Besides the Treatise on Curiosities, what other works did Zhang Hua leave behind?
• What made Emperor Wu of Jin so determined to make his foolish son, the one who asked "Why don't they eat meat porridge?", heir to the throne?


Questions for discussion after the talk:

• Why was the Western Jin unable to sustain stable rule for long?
• Did Zhang Hua hold a consistent political position, and if so, what was it?
• Could Zhang Hua have resolved the conflict between Emperor Hui of Jin's wife and his son (Jia Nanfeng and Crown Prince Minhuai)?
• Why was it so hard to reconcile the divisions between the northern and southern literati of the Western Jin?
• Is there a necessary link between Xuanxue "pure conversation" and empty talk ruining the state?


Related reading:
Fang Xuanling (Tang), Book of Jin
Quan Jiayu, Wei–Jin Politics and the Transmission of Imperial Power
Luo Zongqiang, Xuanxue and the Mentality of Wei–Jin Literati
Qiu Luming, Political Power and Family Networks in the Wei–Jin Transition

intro:

    * Richard Evans, Deng Xiaoping and the Making of Modern China

zh: 别有半生萧瑟
intro:
本次分享将以南梁（北周）文学家庾信及其代表作《哀江南赋》为主题，推其生平以及南北朝后期的部分历史。

一些引起好奇（钓鱼）的问题：
杜甫为何夸李白”清新庾开府，俊逸鲍参军“？
杜甫为何感叹“庾信平生最萧瑟，暮年诗赋动江关”？
庾信的小迷弟杜甫经历了什么才会说“庾信文章老更成”？
何谓“庾信之诗，为梁之冠冕，启唐之先鞭”？
“落霞与孤鹜齐飞，秋水共长天一色”是出自何处？
“春蚕到死丝方尽，蜡炬成灰泪始干”是出自何处？
“可惜流年，忧愁风雨，树犹如此”又是出自何处？
本次将讨论的问题：
南梁的建立和发展经历了怎样的一个过程？
宫体诗和佛教对文化事业分别造成什么样的影响？
南梁如何从歌舞升平迅速走向时局动荡？
侯景之乱如何改变了南北朝格局？
庾信在北周留下什么作品？
庾信的文学成就集中体现在什么地方？
为什么要分享庾信，到今天该如何？
相关资料：
《哀江南赋》
《枯树赋》《小园赋》
《拟咏怀诗二十七首》
《春赋》《马射赋》
《灯赋》《镜赋》《对烛赋》
《周书·王褒庾信传》《北史·庾信传》
田晓菲《烽火与流星》
《雾》
en: Half a Life of Desolation
intro_en:
This session takes as its theme Yu Xin, the writer of the Southern Liang (and later the Northern Zhou), and his masterpiece Lament for the South, tracing his life and part of the history of the late Northern and Southern Dynasties.

Some questions to spark your curiosity (and lure you in):
Why did Du Fu praise Li Bai as "fresh and clear like Yu Kaifu, graceful and free like Bao Canjun"?
Why did Du Fu sigh that "Yu Xin's whole life was most desolate; his poems and rhapsodies in old age stirred the land beyond the passes"?
What did Yu Xin's little fanboy Du Fu go through to say that "Yu Xin's writing grew more accomplished with age"?
What is meant by "Yu Xin's poetry crowns the Liang and leads the way for the Tang"?
Where does "The sunset clouds fly together with a lone wild duck; the autumn waters share one colour with the endless sky" come from?
Where does "The spring silkworm spins silk until it dies; the candle's tears dry only when it burns to ash" come from?
And where does "Alas for the passing years, grieved by wind and rain; even the trees are thus" come from?
Questions we will discuss this time:
How was the Southern Liang founded and how did it develop?
What influence did palace-style poetry and Buddhism each have on cultural life?
How did the Southern Liang go so quickly from peace and revelry to turmoil?
How did the Hou Jing Rebellion change the balance between North and South?
What works did Yu Xin leave in the Northern Zhou?
Where are Yu Xin's literary achievements most concentrated?
Why talk about Yu Xin, and how should we see him today?
Related reading:
Lament for the South
Rhapsody on a Withered Tree; Rhapsody on a Small Garden
Twenty-Seven Poems Imitating "Singing My Thoughts"
Rhapsody on Spring; Rhapsody on Mounted Archery
Rhapsody on the Lamp; Rhapsody on the Mirror; Rhapsody Facing the Candle

zh: 迷惘一代的文学
intro:
“它是奇迹的年代，艺术的年代，过剩的年代，也是讽刺的年代。”

——《爵士时代的回声》，菲茨杰拉德，纽约

1920年代，巴黎充满宽阔大道的重建已过去150年，第二次工业革命完成了近十年，而它的终结——第一次世界大战则刚刚结束。

1920年代，沙龙已存在了两百多年，《心理学原理》出版了30年，“爵士乐”之名刚发明5年。

这是’Jazz Age’, ‘Années folles’, ‘Goldenen Zwanziger’，也是“迷惘的一代”。现代已死，而20年代就是其高峰与灵魂；当代在此，不可避免地建构于其上。

如果你也想见到蝙蝠闪烁的面目、想听到夜的碎片纷扬，如果你也迷惘，那就来吧。雨水中的意象仍待拾起，12节的蓝调还可继续，散文、小说和宣言仍叠在桌上，海明威、艾略特和马里涅提都在等你。

本周五晚，让我们继续百年前的沙龙。

Let us go then, you and I,
When the evening is spread out against the sky
Like a patient etherized upon a table…'

————《普鲁弗洛克的情歌》，艾略特


问题：
用一两句话描述一个令你印象深刻的物体或场景吧。
今年 Met Gala 的主题是《在美国：鎏金年代》，有谁的造型令你印象深刻吗？
分享来自或有关1920年代的一部文艺作品或一位创作者吧。
你如何理解现代性及其与后现代的区别？

简短的参考阅读：
庞德的《在地铁站》（只有两行）
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_a_Station_of_the_Metro
施坦因的《画家们的三幅画像：马蒂斯》
https://www.poetryfoundation.org/poems/55214/matisse
朗斯顿·休斯的《疲劳的蓝调》
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e5G3Q13BL5U
en: The Literature of the Lost Generation
intro_en:
"It was an age of miracles, it was an age of art, it was an age of excess, and it was an age of satire."

—F. Scott Fitzgerald, Echoes of the Jazz Age, New York

In the 1920s, 150 years had passed since Paris was rebuilt with its broad boulevards; the Second Industrial Revolution had been complete for nearly a decade, and its end, the First World War, had only just finished.

In the 1920s, the salon had existed for more than two hundred years, The Principles of Psychology had been out for thirty years, and the name "jazz" had been coined only five years before.

This was the 'Jazz Age', the 'Années folles', the 'Goldenen Zwanziger', and also the "Lost Generation". The modern is dead, and the twenties were its peak and its soul; the contemporary is here, inevitably built upon it.

If you too want to see the flickering faces of bats and hear the fragments of the night scatter, if you too are lost, then come. The images in the rain are still waiting to be picked up, the twelve-bar blues can play on, essays, novels and manifestos are still piled on the table, and Hemingway, Eliot and Marinetti are all waiting for you.

This Friday evening, let us carry on the salon of a hundred years ago.

Let us go then, you and I,
When the evening is spread out against the sky
Like a patient etherized upon a table…'

—T. S. Eliot, The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock

This year's Met Gala theme was "In America: Gilded Glamour". Did anyone's look stand out to you?

How do you understand modernity, and how does it differ from postmodernity?

瘟疫在多大程度上改变了历史？
帝国主义的扩张何种程度影响了医学发展？

intro_en:

To what extent have plagues changed history?
To what extent did imperialist expansion influence the development of medicine?
How did humanity's understanding of germs develop?
Is medicine a profession with moral obligations?
Why do epidemics keep recurring in cycles?

Wan Jinghua, The Road to Conquering Germs

Yamasaki Toyoko, The Great White Tower

对世界产生了怎样的影响？

如何看待20世纪初的整个现代主义运动？

This session will discuss the Modernist movement in architecture in the early twentieth century and the worldwide transformation of architecture it brought about.

What kind of environment gives rise to change?

What does modern architecture stand for?

What impact did it have on the world?

How should we view the Modernist movement of the early twentieth century as a whole?

zh: 淮泗驰急流
intro:

淮泗流域是如何形成的？
淮泗地区在历史上发挥过什么样的作用？

en: Swift Currents of the Huai and Si
intro_en:
This session will discuss the development and changes of the Huai–Si river basin centred on Xuzhou, and their effects today.
How was the Huai–Si basin formed?
What role has the Huai–Si region played in history?
Why have rebellions and revolutions so often broken out in this region?
How have changing hydrological conditions, including shifts in the course of the Yellow River, affected the region's ecology?
How have history and geography shaped people's economic lives?

zh: 中唐的棱镜：平卢镇节度使
intro:
本次分享将讨论盛唐到中唐这一时期平卢镇节度使这一政治军事团体的设立，迁徙和兴衰。

该怎么看待割据的藩镇？
如何看待唐代藩镇制度与拜占庭军区制的异同？

唐代的东北边疆是什么样的？

安史之乱后的唐朝是怎么维持住的？
平卢军为何会从平叛的主力变成唐廷的心腹大患？
相比其他藩镇，平卢军有什么特点？


参考内容：

Questions to think about beforehand:
Were the military governorships a failed institution?
How should we view the separatist military provinces?
How do the Tang military provinces compare with the Byzantine theme system?

In the talk we will discuss:
What was the Tang's northeastern frontier like?
How was An Lushan able to gain enormous power on the northeastern frontier?
How did the Tang hold together after the An Lushan Rebellion?
Why did the Pinglu Army go from being the main force in suppressing the rebellion to a grave threat to the Tang court?
Compared with other military provinces, what was distinctive about the Pinglu Army?

Feng Wanshi, A Policy Response on Frontier Affairs
Yang Xiaoyan, The Pinglu Army of the Tang and the Bohai Rim Region

2.高等教育和基础教育哪个更重要？
3.公立学校和私立学校，在招生、经费、政策、性质上有何不同？
4.历史上的私立办学，都遭遇过哪些困难？
5.不同的国家，私立大学有何区别和前景？

intro_en:
We plan to hold four sessions on Japanese history in the coming weeks, themed around NHK's 2013 taiga drama Yae's Cherry Blossoms (Yae no Sakura).
(I) The Black Ships and the Turmoil of the Shogunate
(II) Aizu Domain and the Boshin War
(III) The Meiji Restoration and the Satsuma Rebellion
(Finale) Niijima Jō and Dōshisha University

1. What can we learn from the history of Dōshisha University?
2. Which matters more, higher education or basic education?
3. How do public and private schools differ in admissions, funding, policy and nature?
4. What difficulties have private schools faced in history?

zh: 胡塞尔与现象学
intro:
大家好，本周五将由John为大家分享他所学过的现象学。这个话题在很多方面值得深挖，让人着迷。我们将关注它的创始人埃德蒙·胡塞尔和他的学派发展动因。他和上周讨论的两位艺术家（马勒和卡夫卡）生活在同一时代，并且拥有相似的背景，所以我们会和上次分享联动。即使错过了上周分享，本次仍能在哲学领域有新的思考。

本次活动以英语进行。下面是一些启发性的问题：

1.你是否赞同我们应当回到“经验”中寻找逻辑规律？
2.你是否相信心理学是一套不连贯的理论？或者说，心理学它是否是“合理的”科学理论的一部分？
3.假设我们的意识是“有意的”，对于人工智能的反驳是“计算机没有任何形式（像人类一样）的‘意向性’”。这是对人工智能项目的一个令人信服的批判吗？
4.在上周所讨论的马勒和卡夫卡的想法中，哪些也适用于胡塞尔？胡塞尔的哲学理论对于其他艺术或者文学又造成何种启发？
en: Husserl and Phenomenology
intro_en:
Hello everyone. This Friday, John will share what he has learned about phenomenology. It is a fascinating topic that rewards deep exploration in many ways. We will focus on its founder, Edmund Husserl, and the forces that drove the development of his school. He lived at the same time as the two artists we discussed last week (Mahler and Kafka) and came from a similar background, so this session will link up with the last one. Even if you missed last week's session, you can still come away with new thoughts on philosophy.

This session will be held in English. Here are some questions to get you thinking:

1. Do you agree that we should return to "experience" to find the laws of logic?
2. Do you believe psychology is an incoherent set of theories? Or, put another way, is psychology part of "sound" scientific theory?
3. Suppose our consciousness is "intentional"; the objection to artificial intelligence is that "computers have no form of 'intentionality' (as humans do)". Is this a convincing critique of the AI project?
4. Which of the ideas of Mahler and Kafka discussed last week also apply to Husserl? And what inspiration has Husserl's philosophy offered to other arts or literature?

zh: 马勒与卡夫卡
intro:
本次分享将围绕作曲家马勒与作家卡夫卡的背景、作品，对于他们的思想、身份认同进行有趣的讨论。问题如下：

1.为何把马勒和卡夫卡放在一起讨论？难道是因为“作家”和“作曲家”仅有一字之差吗？
2.作为音乐家的马勒和作家的卡夫卡有何共性？
3.如何看待马勒交响作品中的断裂与意识形态攻伐？
4.如何理解卡夫卡的写作理念和作品中的隐喻？
5.在马勒和卡夫卡的作品中如何加入中国文化元素？对待中国文化，他们采取了什么样的态度？

大家对于马勒/卡夫卡的印象是什么？或者更大的说，大家对于德国/捷克的印象是什么？
en: Mahler and Kafka
intro_en:
This session will explore the backgrounds and works of the composer Mahler and the writer Kafka, with a lively discussion of their thought and sense of identity. The questions are as follows:

1. Why discuss Mahler and Kafka together? Is it just because "writer" and "composer" differ by only one character in Chinese?
2. What do Mahler the musician and Kafka the writer have in common?
3. What do you make of the ruptures and ideological clashes in Mahler's symphonic works?
4. How should we understand Kafka's ideas about writing and the metaphors in his work?
5. How did Mahler and Kafka bring elements of Chinese culture into their work? What attitude did they take towards Chinese culture?

What are your impressions of Mahler and Kafka? Or, more broadly, what are your impressions of Germany and the Czech lands?

zh: 大宋奇男子 - 章惇
intro:
本次分享围绕北宋后期的政治家章惇，讲述有关他那些有趣有料甚至令人瞳孔地震的故事（段子）。结合王安石变法的背景故事，对于北宋后期历史的叙事文本被制造/解读/传播进行思考。将讨论以下几个问题：

1.王安石变法造成了什么影响？南宋以降人们是如何看待变法和北宋灭亡的？
2.这些认识塑造了何种偏见，对于历史叙述造成了什么样的影响？
3.章惇和王安石之间是什么关系？新党在变法过程扮演了什么角色？
4.苏轼和章惇是什么关系？为何会发展到相爱相杀?
5.这种历史塑造，今天对我们有什么启示？

此外，在分享开始前，为大家提供一个便于在自我介绍阶段讨论的问题：

对于宋朝，尤其是北宋，大家的印象是什么？
en: Zhang Dun, the Remarkable Man of Song
intro_en:
This session centres on Zhang Dun, the statesman of the late Northern Song, telling fun, juicy and even jaw-dropping stories (anecdotes) about him. Against the background of Wang Anshi's reforms, we will reflect on how the narrative texts of late Northern Song history were produced, interpreted and circulated. We will discuss the following questions:

1. What were the effects of Wang Anshi's reforms? How did people from the Southern Song onward view the reforms and the fall of the Northern Song?
2. What biases did these views create, and how did they affect historical narratives?
3. What was the relationship between Zhang Dun and Wang Anshi? What role did the New Policies faction play in the reforms?
4. What was the relationship between Su Shi and Zhang Dun? How did it turn into a love-hate relationship?
5. What does this shaping of history teach us today?

In addition, before the talk begins, here is a question for everyone to discuss during the introductions:

What are your impressions of the Song dynasty, especially the Northern Song?

zh: 建安文学一瞥
intro:
本次分享主题属于中国古典文学，也涉及历史范畴。将讨论以下几个问题：

1.什么是建安文学？建安文学有何特色？代表性人物有谁？
2.谁定义了建安文学？它又如何成为后世效仿和神往的经典？
3.建安文学中的重要人物“三曹”“七子”之间有着怎样的互动？他们之间存在什么样的关系？
4.东汉末年的瘟疫对文学创作造成了什么影响？
5.作为建安文学的代表性作品，曹植《洛神赋》是否如传言所说，是写给曹丕的妻子甄氏？曹丕和曹植兄弟之间到底是什么样的感情态度？

此外，在分享开始前，为大家提供一个便于在自我介绍阶段讨论的问题：

如果在三国时代人物中选择一位交朋友，你会选择谁？
en: A Glimpse of Jian'an Literature
intro_en:
This session's topic belongs to classical Chinese literature and also touches on history. We will discuss the following questions:

1. What is Jian'an literature? What are its distinctive features? Who are its representative figures?
2. Who defined Jian'an literature? And how did it become a classic that later generations imitated and admired?
3. How did the key figures of Jian'an literature, the "Three Caos" and the "Seven Masters", interact? What were their relationships with one another?
4. How did the plague at the end of the Eastern Han affect literary creation?
5. As a representative work of Jian'an literature, was Cao Zhi's Rhapsody on the Goddess of the Luo really written for Cao Pi's wife, Lady Zhen, as rumour has it? What were the true feelings between the brothers Cao Pi and Cao Zhi?

In addition, before the talk begins, here is a question for everyone to discuss during the introductions:

If you could befriend one figure from the Three Kingdoms period, whom would you choose?
